Join us, and be part of what's next.
**IN A NUTSHELL**
As a sports nutrition and health food manufacturer, we produce a wide range of products including powders, capsules, tablets and soft gels within our own manufacturing facility.
In this shift based role, you will be working closely with the operations team to ensure every product released to customers meets our Food Safety and Quality Standards. Reporting to the UK Site Quality Assurance Manager, you will be responsible for monitoring Food Safety and Quality within manufacturing that support our programs for BRC implementation.
**WHAT WILL YOU BE DOING?**
**Quality control and product release**
* Carry out quality control checks during production, including CCP monitoring, label verification, weights and review of shift documentation.
* Complete line clearance and start-up checks before production begins, including verification of allergen changeovers.
* Carry out in-process checks appropriate to each product format (e.g. capsule and tablet weights.
* Verify metal detection and foreign body controls at the required frequency.
* Carry out hygiene and cleaning verification (e.g. ATP swabbing).
* Complete organoleptic assessment of finished product against specification.
* Conduct environmental monitoring and product sampling in line with quality management system requirements, and record results accurately.
* Manage product under positive release, making sure it is held until results are approved and released in line with the release procedure.
* Place product on hold where it does not meet specification or where food safety or quality is at risk, [including stopping production where necessary].
* Make sure all stock on hold or in quarantine is resolved within specified timeframes, in line with the hold and release procedure.
* Keep retained production samples organised, labelled and easy to locate.
**Non-conformances and complaints**
* Raise non-conformances and support manufacturing with investigations, including root cause analysis.
* Support the QA Manager with customer complaint investigations by gathering evidence, identifying likely root causes and following up agreed corrective actions.
**Audits and compliance**
* Carry out internal audits in line with the audit schedule (e.g. glass and brittle plastics, GMP, knife, pen, traceability).
* Support external, customer and certification audits.
* Maintain calibration of Technical equipment in line with the calibration schedule.
* Keep traceability records accurate and up to date, and support traceability exercises.
* Coach production teammates on GMP, hygiene and allergen standards on the shop floor.
* Make sure HACCP, food safety standards and internal quality procedures are followed across manufacturing.
**Continuous improvement**
* Identify and suggest improvements to food safety and quality systems and processes within the manufacturing facility.
* Undertake other reasonable duties as required by the QA Manage
* Conduct environmental monitoring and product sampling in line with quality management system requirements and ensure results are reported accurately.
* To ensure there is control of product samples under positive release
* Complete organoleptic assessment of the final product to ensure the product meets specification.
* Responsible for investigating and analysing customer complaints, identifying root causes and implementing corrective actions to ensure customer satisfaction and product quality.
* Raise non-conformances and support manufacturing with any investigations related to non-conformances including investigations linked to customer complaints.
* Carry out internal audits as per schedule (e.g. glass, GMP, knife, pen, traceability)
* Ensure calibration of equipment linked to Technical is maintained according to the calibration schedule.
* Ensure retained production samples are sorted in a tidy manner and are easily identifiable.
* Assist with traceability records keeping.
* Actively suggest improvements in the current food safety and quality systems and processes within the manufacturing facility.
* Ensure all stock placed on hold/quarantine is resolved in a quick and efficient manner.
* To support the QA manager as required.
* Ensure compliance with HACCP, food safety standards and internal quality protocols.
**WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR?**
**HARD SKILLS / EXPERIENCE / QUALIFICATIONS:**
* Level 2 Food Safety and Level 2 HACCP, or equivalent.
* Previous experience in a quality assurance or quality control role within food, supplement or pharmaceutical manufacturing.
* Working knowledge of GMP and HACCP principles.
* Computer literate, with experience of [Microsoft Office / Google Workspace].
**SOFT SKILLS / PERSONALITY TRAITS:**
* Strong attention to detail and accurate record keeping.
* Confident in communicating with production teams, including challenging when standards are not met.
* Able to manage multiple tasks, prioritise and meet deadlines
**NICE-TO-HAVES:**
* Level 3 Food Safety and/or Level 3 HACCP.
* Experience working to BRCGS or another GFSI-recognised standard.
* Internal auditor training.
* Experience using root cause analysis tools (e.g. 5 Whys, fishbone).
**WHAT ARE THE GAINS?**
* A day off to celebrate your **Birthday** 🎂
* **PerkBox** Subscription 👍
* **60% discount** on all **Bulk**TM products 💰
* Teammate **Pension** Scheme 💰
* **Life Assurance 💟**
* **Medicash 👩‍⚕️**
* A day off for **Volunteering** (optional) 🤗
* **Cycle to Work Scheme 🚲**
* Enhanced **Maternity & Paternity leave 🐣**and workplace **nursery scheme 🧒**
* **Bulk**TM **Pantry 🍴**
* **Happy Hour** Drinks Fridge (Thursdays & Fridays) 🎉
**LOCATION**: **Colchester, UK**

# Engineering Manager - Distributed Systems, Python / Go
Home Based - Americas; Home based - EMEA
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, as well as industry leaders across many sectors.
Canonical is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1,200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.
The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.
We are hiring an **Engineering Manager for Distributed Systems Testing** to lead a team responsible for the quality engineering platform that enables deployment and validation of distributed systems across Canonical's cloud portfolio.
We see quality engineering as a first-class engineering practice. Our Distributed Systems Testing team ensures the performance, correctness, resilience and interoperability of Canonical cloud solutions built with technologies such as Juju, Terraform, OpenStack and Kubernetes. These systems are deployed and tested across diverse environments, from bare-metal to the public cloud.
As Engineering Manager, you will combine strong software engineering judgement with people leadership. You will develop engineering talent, establish effective engineering practices, shape technical direction with senior engineers, and ensure the team delivers high-quality testing infrastructure and automation that enables engineering teams across Canonical to ship software with confidence.
We believe engineering managers should be outstanding engineers themselves. You should be comfortable reviewing patches, evaluating software design, debugging a distributed system, or discussing test architecture. You will contribute technically where appropriate to set a high standard, while recognizing that your greatest impact comes from shaping the direction, focus, effectiveness, and growth of the whole team.
You will work closely with senior engineers and engineering leaders across Canonical to define priorities, improve testing capabilities, and advance how we validate increasingly complex cloud-native and distributed systems.
**Location:** This is a globally remote role, typically leading a team concentrated within a major time zone such as EMEA or the Americas.
## **What you'll do**
* Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of software and quality engineers, ranging from graduate to senior level
* Set clear expectations, strengthen engineering practices, and ensure timely delivery against agreed goals
* Partner with senior engineers to shape technical strategy, architecture, roadmap, and engineering standards
* Guide the development of automated testing infrastructure for the reliability, interoperability, and resilience of distributed systems
* Improve CI pipelines, testing tools, and reporting used to validate Canonical's products and solutions across bare-metal, private and public cloud environments
* Enable engineering teams across Canonical to adopt effective distributed-systems testing practices and tooling
* Contribute technical leadership through design and code reviews, debugging, and hands-on engineering where appropriate
* Represent the team with stakeholders and collaborate across Canonical on quality engineering, infrastructure, and developer experience
## **What we're looking for in you**
* An exceptional academic track record from both high school and university
* Experience in leading, coaching, and mentoring software engineers
* Professional software engineering experience with Python or Go
* Expertise in distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, quality engineering, or a closely related domain
* Strong knowledge of modern software testing processes, strategies, and automation
* Experience with Linux (Debian or Ubuntu preferred)
* Strong technical judgement and the ability to engage meaningfully in code reviews, architecture discussions, and software design
* Experience working in an agile development environment with the ability to organize a team to deliver high-quality results
* Professional written and spoken English with excellent communication and presentation skills
* Great interpersonal skills, curiosity, flexibility, and accountability, demonstrating passion, thoughtfulness, and self-motivation
* Ability to travel twice a year, for company events up to two weeks each
## **Additional skills we value**
Experience with any of the following:
* Cloud technologies such as Kubernetes, OpenStack, Juju, Terraform, AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure
* Designing testing strategies for distributed or cloud-native systems
* Building or operating large-scale CI/CD and test infrastructure
* Applying AI or machine learning to test analysis, failure classification, or engineering workflows
* Deploying, operating, or debugging distributed systems
* Leading globally distributed teams
## **What we offer colleagues**
We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually, and more often for graduates and associates, to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus.
We provide all team members with additional benefits that reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programmes to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.
* Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person
* Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
* Annual compensation review
* Recognition rewards
* Annual holiday leave
* Maternity and paternity leave
* Employee Assistance Programme and wellness support
* Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues
* Priority Pass and travel upgrades for long-haul company events
## **About Canonical**
Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and a leading platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software.
We recruit globally and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004. Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.
### **Canonical is an equal opportunity employer**
We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

## About the role
Our customers are building AI products where a wrong value is not an embarrassment but a harm: a missed allergen, an exercise that aggravates an injury, a drug interaction not flagged. They do not need another vector database. They need to be able to say, with evidence, why a value is what it is.
This role decides what we build next for them. That means talking to those teams, understanding the field that actually has to be right, and turning it into slices an engineer can start on Monday, including the acceptance criteria for what must fail closed and what must be provable from a receipt.
The scarce skill here is saying no. The product surface wants to widen constantly (more input formats, more connectors, more knobs) and most of that should wait until the current slice is honest.
## What you'd do
* Talk to teams building on safety-critical catalogs and turn what you hear into slices an engineer can start on Monday
* Own the pipeline end to end as a product: inputs, contracts, curation, release, the deployed tool and its security settings
* Write the acceptance criteria, including what must fail closed and what must be provable from a receipt
* Say no to work that widens the surface before the current slice is honest
* Keep the public roadmap and the site accurate about what is built versus what is planned
## What we need
* Four or more years in product, at least some of it on a technical or developer-facing product
* You can read an API contract and hold your own in a design discussion with engineers
* You write specs that are specific enough to argue with, including the edge cases
* You have killed or cut a feature you liked, and can explain the call
* Comfortable enough with SQL to answer your own questions about usage
## Nice to have, not required
* Background in data quality, catalog management, search or retrieval
* You have worked with a regulated customer and survived a security review
* You have written developer documentation people actually used
## How we work
* Small team, thin slices, shipped weekly. Nothing sits on a branch for a month.
* Reviews are real. Every feature ships with its tests, and a bug found in review is cheaper than one found by a customer.
* Safety-critical means the boring answer usually wins: fail closed, keep the receipt, don't guess.
* We only claim what ships. That applies to the product, the roadmap and the offer letter.

You will own a set of data products, be accountable for their quality, and be the person who turns a customer problem into a clear, buildable product that people genuinely want to use. * The delivery roadmap for your products - what you build, in what order, and what you deliberately leave out.

**What This Role Will Do** 1. **Data product ownership and delivery**
* Own the product development cycle for your data products, from discovery and validation through to launch, adoption, and iteration.
* Define requirements, set priorities, and make clear scope calls - what a product should and should not do, and why.
* Work closely with data engineering and data science to shape data assets that can be delivered at the highest quality - so customers can build on data they trust - across CRMs, APIs, and agentic systems.
* Ground every product decision in a customer use case and a commercial outcome, not just technical capability.
* Define the success metrics and KPIs for your products up front, then measure outcomes continuously - using the data to drive decisions and iterate.
* Shape how your products are packaged and priced - working with commercial teams so the way data is offered matches how customers buy and where they see value.
1. **Customer understanding**
* Turn customer needs into clear data requirements that engineering and data teams can build against.
* Validate that what you build creates value - decide up front how you will know a product is working, and test it with real customers.
* Partner with Sales and Customer Success so customers realise the value of the data, and feed what you learn back into the product.
1. **Data quality and governance**
* Own the quality of the data assets in your area and set the standard customers can rely on.
* Decide how to surface confidence, freshness, and match quality to customers where it affects trust and adoption.
* Build GDPR compliance and data governance into the product from the start.
* Put evaluation frameworks in place - specific to data products - to measure data quality objectively and improve it continuously, so you can prove the data meets the standard customers rely on.
* Work with data sourcing teams to expand and strengthen the datasets behind your products - deciding what to source, build, or partner for.
1. **Stakeholder Management**
* Act as the primary point of contact for your product area across Engineering, Data Science, Sales, Customer Success, Commercial, and Compliance — translating between technical and commercial language as needed.
* Manage dependencies with product peers who own adjacent surfaces; where priorities conflict, resolve disagreements directly and drive to a decision without escalation unless necessary.

* Build trust with customer-facing teams (Sales, CS) so they can represent your product accurately and feed real customer signal back into your roadmap.

* Use that view to sharpen your products and spot where Cognism's data can create differentiated value.

You understand how data and models work, lead with curiosity about the customer, and land with real outcomes. **Must-Haves** * 5+ years in product roles, with direct experience owning data products or data-driven features in a B2B SaaS or technology business.
* Proven ability to define and own data use cases - mapping customer segments, workflows, and outcomes into a clear product direction.
* Experience setting product strategy for an area you own - deciding where to focus, what to bet on, and what to say no to.
* Direct experience treating data as a product: you have defined a data offering, built it, brought it to market, and can speak to the impact.

# Retail Engineer (Deployment Strategist), UK
London, United Kingdom
Full-time
CommerceClarity is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on what you can do and how you work with people.
## What the role is about
Retailers still run too much catalog work through spreadsheets and copy-paste: filling missing attributes, adapting products to each marketplace, and keeping thousands of SKUs accurate. CommerceClarity replaces that manual work with AI agents.
As a Retail Engineer you put those agents to work inside each customer’s operation, from discovery and workflow design to integration and production. Part retail consultant, part engineer, working with our customers across the UK.
This is a high-ownership seat. You own our most strategic accounts end to end and you set the delivery method the rest of the team runs on. We weigh attitude and the combination over years on paper: the sweet spot is three to six years, and the right builder energy beats seniority.
This is one of the first seats we are opening in the UK. You would work out of the London hub on UK accounts, with the platform and the delivery method already built behind you in Milan and Barcelona.
## A job that did not exist three years ago
New tools tend to produce job titles that were not there a few years earlier. Growth engineer and marketing engineer both appeared once the people who understood the funnel could write the code that ran it, and forward deployed engineer and deployment strategist appeared when the same thing happened to enterprise delivery. None of them was a rename. They exist because splitting the person who understands the process from the person who builds it stopped paying for itself.
Retail Engineer is that seat for catalog operations. Outside retail the same job is called deployment strategist, and most of the people who fit it have spent five or six years in solution delivery or solution consulting at a retail software vendor or a consultancy. They read business processes for a living and they own the customer, and almost all of them have a technical side they were never given room to use: the configuration screen ended exactly where the interesting part started, and everything past it went to a development team on another continent.
What changed is the platform. The agents are built there, changed there and run there, so the person who designs the workflow is the person who builds it, in front of the customer, in the same week. You write the prompts and you wire up their systems, and when a number moves you go and change whatever produced it. AI coding assistants work alongside you, so a change that used to take a sprint becomes a prompt and a test.
The half of the job you were already good at stays. Discovery, a room full of stakeholders, an account that trusts you: here that is what keeps the building honest, because you are the one who heard what they actually meant. What you gain is the other half. You spend your days on agent design, evals and prompt engineering, inside a company that runs its own operations on agents, which is a faster education in this than anything you could sign up for.
## Why this role is different
It is not pure delivery and it is not pure engineering. You sit at the intersection: you understand the retailer’s catalog workflow well enough to redesign it around agents, and you have the depth to build the agent flows yourself.
You cover the whole lifecycle. The preparation, mapping their processes, designing the workflow, writing and iterating the prompts, defining the KPIs. Then the run, deployment, integration with their systems, monitoring, debugging, and optimization against those KPIs.
And you do not only deliver. You shape how we deliver and you grow the engineers around you, so one senior hire lifts the team instead of adding a pair of hands. You work closely with the Agent Product Managers, who own the product direction, and with the AI Engineers on delivery.
## What you would do
* Lead agent implementations end to end for enterprise retailers, from kickoff to production, on our DIPE method: design, implement, prove, evolve.
* Own our most strategic accounts and the heaviest proofs of concept directly.
* Define the success KPIs with the customer, and build the measurement loop that proves the agents are working.

job_description:
## Senior Product Designer, The New Yorker
Apply
: The Adelphi, London, GB

Condé Nast is one of the world's most renowned media publishing companies, creating and distributing every type of media today, spanning print and digital publishing in all formats. With a portfolio of some of today's most influential brands, the company continues to grow its audience through a global operational and content infrastructure across its 12 owned and operated markets. Headquartered in New York City, the company's owned and operated markets include China, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, Mexico & Latin America, Spain, Taiwan, UAE/Dubai, the U.K., and the U.S., with additional local license partners in over twenty additional markets across the globe. Lead brands include Vogue, The New Yorker, GQ, Architectural Digest, Condé Nast Traveler, Vanity Fair, Wired, Allure, Ars Technica, Bon Appétit, House & Garden, Pitchfork, Tatler, and Vogue Business.
# **Job Description**
Location:
London, GB
**Condé Nast thrives on collaboration, and our teams come together in the office four days a week (Monday - Thursday).**
We value diversity of background, views and cultures. We celebrate people for their personal qualities, skills and contributions, recognising the power our brands have to influence and shape culture.
The New Yorker brings a distinctive editorial voice to everything it creates. Our goal is to build a stronger, more habitual relationship with our readers, making reading and play a valued part of their everyday lives. Across The New Yorker’s digital experiences and our Puzzles & Games offering, you’ll help give people compelling reasons to return: something worth reading, listening to or watching, a satisfying game, and thoughtful connections between visits.
We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer to help shape these experiences across web and apps. Your work will span games themselves and the experiences around them, from gameplay and feedback to discovery, onboarding and the journeys that bring readers and players back. You’ll combine strong visual and interaction craft with clear product thinking, taking a key role in progressing initiatives from early exploration through launch and iteration. You’ll work closely with design leads, product managers, engineers, researchers and editorial partners to turn open questions into considered, usable products.
We’re also evolving how we design and build. You’ll bring curiosity and familiarity with AI tools, with room to develop your skills in prototyping and working more directly with code as part of the role.
## What you'll be doing
Connecting reading and play to lasting habits You design both games and the experiences around them, exploring and refining gameplay alongside discovery, onboarding, progress and returning to play. You connect this work to the wider reader experience, considering how each interaction builds familiarity, enjoyment and reasons to return. You question assumptions and work with your partners to define what is worth solving and how you’ll know it has worked.
Bringing editorial character to digital experiences You translate distinctive brand identities into clear, engaging interfaces. You bring care to typography, hierarchy, layout and interaction, balancing the character of the brand with usability, accessibility and the needs of different devices.
Making interaction feel right You use prototypes to explore behaviour, timing, motion and feedback. Whether you’re refining a reading journey, helping someone discover a game or developing an interaction within one, you pay attention to the details that make an experience intuitive and satisfying.
Understanding readers and players You seek out research, analytics and direct feedback to inform your decisions. You run lightweight usability testing, partnering with UX Research where deeper investigation is needed, and use what you learn to improve the work.
Designing with and contributing to systems You use shared components, patterns and design tokens confidently, recognising where consistency helps and where a new approach is justified. You contribute reusable solutions that support brand expression and work within the realities of our platforms.
Staying close to implementation You collaborate with engineers throughout the design process, discussing feasibility early and reviewing the experience as it is built. You work through interaction details, edge cases and visual QA so the quality of the shipped product reflects the intent of the design.
Using AI as part of your practice You explore where AI tools can add value to your design practice, building on your experience and learning alongside the team. You experiment with ways to develop ideas, prototype and collaborate with engineering, applying your judgement to the results and sharing what you learn.
Learning from what ships You agree intended outcomes with your product and engineering partners, then use analytics and qualitative feedback to understand performance. You connect design decisions to measures such as engagement, repeat use and retention, and identify where further iteration will make a difference.
Contributing to the team You communicate your thinking clearly, build productive relationships across disciplines and participate actively in critique. You share your work and methods, support other designers and bring an open, constructive approach to feedback.
## You'll thrive in this role if...
* You bring strong visual and interaction design skills, with particular care for typography, detail and the quality of the finished experience.
* You can take an ambiguous problem and turn it into a clear direction, working with others to make sensible decisions about scope and priorities.
* You’re interested in editorial products, puzzles and games, and what makes people return to an experience over time.
* You’re confident in Figma and interactive prototyping, and comfortable working with design systems, tokens and technical constraints.
* You’re familiar with AI tools, have used them in your design practice and are curious about developing your approach further.
* You use research and data to inform decisions, alongside a clear design point of view.
* You build strong relationships with product, engineering and editorial partners, and can explain your reasoning to people with different perspectives.
* You take ownership of your work while seeking feedback early and recognising when a decision needs wider alignment.
* You’re comfortable applying your skills to different brands and problem spaces as the team’s priorities evolve.
## What success looks like
In your first six months, you’ll have developed an understanding of our readers, players, brands and platforms, and built effective relationships with your immediate partners. You’ll have taken a key role in shaping and delivering a meaningful initiative, with responsibility for progressing the design and room to influence its direction, working closely with the design lead. Your prototypes and design decisions will help the team resolve questions and move forward with confidence.
By the end of your first year, you’ll have carried initiatives through launch and iteration, with evidence of what improved for users and what the team learned. You’ll be a trusted partner who can independently move work forward, maintain a high standard through implementation and contribute useful patterns and practices to the wider design team.
## What we'd like to see
We’re looking for a portfolio that shows your contribution to real digital products, the decisions you made and how the work developed. In particular:
* Visual and interaction craft — thoughtful typography, hierarchy and composition, alongside considered behaviours, transitions and feedback.
* Product judgement — how you framed a problem, explored alternatives and made trade-offs based on user needs, evidence and delivery constraints.
* Connected experiences — how your work fits into a wider journey and helps people discover value, continue an activity or return.
* Brand sensitivity — how you express a distinctive identity while creating an accessible, usable experience.
* Prototyping and experimentation — how you made ideas tangible and used prototypes or testing to answer meaningful questions.
* Implementation quality — how you worked with engineers to resolve details and maintain quality through to production.
* Outcomes and learning — what happened after launch, what you learned and how that informed your next decisions.
Experience designing consumer digital products is particularly relevant. Editorial, subscription, puzzles or games experience would be valuable, but isn’t essential.
Experience: Typically 5+ years in product or interaction design, or equivalent experience demonstrated through your work.
## About Condé Nast Technology
Condé Nast Technology builds the products, systems and experiences that power our brands, including Vogue, The New Yorker, GQ, WIRED and Vanity Fair. Our work supports creativity and business growth across publishing, loyalty and commerce.
We’re a global team of designers, engineers, product managers and researchers. We’re investing in a design culture built on strong craft, thoughtful collaboration and a willingness to explore better ways of working.
If this role sounds like a good fit but you don’t meet every criterion, we’d still like to hear from you.
**What benefits do we offer?**
* 25 days holiday (plus bank holidays) and extra days of annual leave if you move house or want to volunteer.
* You’ll have access to a competitive pension scheme, Bupa Private Healthcare, Season ticket loans and eye tests.
* We offer a range of tools to support your wellbeing, including core hours, 10 remote days (from home or a country with a Condé Nast office location), access to our Employee Assistance Programme, corporate gym membership and cycle to work scheme.
* We’re a dog friendly office, plus you’ll enjoy discounts and magazine subscriptions, keeping you up to date with all things Condé Nast.
* We encourage personal and professional growth through the Condé Nast Learning Hub where you’ll find an extensive portfolio of learning courses and training, available in local languages.
* Our Employee Resource Groups provide a platform for employees to identify shared objectives, exchange ideas, and work on community priorities for our global workforce.
# **What happens next?**
If you are interested in this opportunity, please apply below, and we will review your application as soon as possible. You can update your resume or upload a cover letter at any time by accessing your candidate profile.
***Condé Nast is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, age, familial status and other legally protected characteristics.***

At Confirm, we’re building what’s next in workforce enablement. We connect the dots between learning, engagement and performance, using intelligent technology, content and data to help organisations unlock the potential of their people.
We’re a growing, global team where people are trusted to make an impact, take ownership and grow. We are looking for a commercially savvy, forward-facing Product Manager to spearhead the growth of our leading-edge learning product. This is a "zero-to-one" opportunity where you will be responsible for defining the market fit for a highly innovative product that bridges the gap between generative AI and meaningful learning and enablement outcomes, delivering a product ready for the world’s largest and most innovative brands and users.
Unlike product management roles focused on backlog maintenance, this position is highly commercial and external. You will be the face of the product—partnering with our revenue teams, engaging directly with clients, and representing Confirm at major industry events. While you live at the leading edge of AI, every decision you make is anchored in robust learning or enablement theory to ensure we deliver a fantastic, high-performing product, not just a set of AI experiments.
**What You Will Be Doing**
Roles and responsibilities include:
* Market Shaping & Product-Market Fit: Work tirelessly to identify and secure Product-Market Fit, iterating based on rapid feedback loops from early adopters and the competitive landscape.
* Product Advocacy & Enablement: Act as the primary subject matter expert for our Sales, Account Management, and Customer Success teams, providing them with the narrative and tools needed to win.
* Client Engagement: Lead high-stakes discovery sessions and demonstrations with clients, translating complex AI capabilities into tangible business value. You will use deep customer insights to make the hard trade-off decisions. You aren't just listening to clients; you are deciding which features will drive the product forward and which are distractions.
* Innovation Intelligence: Maintain a deep, relevant understanding of AI (LLMs, agents, and multi-modalities), staying ahead of limitations and opportunities within rapidly changing technology.
* Learning-First Design: Ensure the product isn't just an exercise in AI innovation and ensure that learning theory is built into the core user experience.
* UX Stewardship: Partner with designers to ensure the interface is world-class, intuitive, and reflects the leading-edge nature of the tech that is ready to be used by the world’s largest brands and hyperscalers alike.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:
* Innovation with intent: You can live within the messiness of a zero-to-one product innovating at high-speed and can convert this into a solid and stable BAU state as the product moves into production, adoption and maturity.
* AI Fluency: You have a deep, practical understanding of current AI models and concepts. You understand the "foibles" (hallucinations, latency, token costs) as well as the opportunities for transformative UX. You know where AI is strong and where it can mislead. You verify outputs and keep decision-quality high.
* Pedagogical Depth: You have experience in learning design, enablement or educational theory. You understand how people actually learn by drawing on influences from leading commentators and theorists and the best examples of real-world implementation, and can apply this to AI-driven product.
* Commercial Instinct: You have a proven track record of supporting revenue growth, enabling sales teams, and navigating the nuances of B2B SaaS commercial cycles. You are measured on product adoption and successful delivery to high standards, not just lead generation or 'hype'.
* Strategic Communication: You are a natural "evangelist" who is comfortable on stage, on camera, or in a boardroom.
* Problem focussed: You prefer problem-solving, customer insight and advocacy over granular ticket management and backlog grooming.
* Visual Eye: You have a refined sense of "what good looks like" in modern software design and won't settle for mediocre user experiences.

We build a horizontal platform made up of composable primitives, not feature-by-feature point solutions, and we take the same approach to design—especially on Web.

You'll own that surface end to end alongside Shaked Ginott, our Lead Web Designer — just the two of you, which means scope and seniority grow as fast as you can carry them. You'll design and build on it directly and be accountable for how what you ship performs in the market, working closely with product, commercial, marketing, brand, and SEO.
On a daily basis, you'll:
* Turn briefs from commercial, product, and marketing into pages that ship—across a breadth of styles including platform verticals, campaign support, product release pages and SEO infrastructure
* Design and build in components, rules, and the CMS rather than one-off pages, so changes compound across the site as brand and positioning evolve
* Monitor and maintain performance, find and fix bugs, and QA changes before they reach the live site
## Why come in-house?
The strongest web talent usually gets pulled toward agencies. We think the better work is here. At an agency you hand a project off and move to the next client; in-house, you own one surface for years and your work compounds as the brand and positioning evolve.
You sit inside the business, close to product and go-to-market, so the work is shaped by company strategy and measured on commercial results rather than sign-off. Studio Planhat runs with the discipline of a research team more than a traditional creative shop: brand here is built through cumulative effort over years, not campaigns over quarters. The line from what you ship to what it does in the market is short, and it's yours to close.
## Competencies
To succeed in this role:
* You design in components and rules, not one-off instances, and you tidy as you go — you're impatient with fixes that solve one page and don't scale
* You have a clear eye for what's right and what's nearly right, and you can say what's missing and fix it yourself
* You reach for frontier technologies (e.g., code-gen, generative design, self-built apps and tools) early and build repeatable ways of working with them rather than prompting ad hoc
* You question decisions that were settled before you arrived, learn fast, and give and take feedback directly
Technically, you must be:
* familiar with building sites in a no-/low-code web builder such as Framer or Webflow — you understand components, variants, responsive behaviour, and publishing
* able to show a portfolio of aesthetically tight and systematically robust web work you've designed, built, and shipped
* comfortable enough with the HTML and CSS underneath to understand what the builder produces, rather than just prompting for it
* fluent with AI tools and excited to stay hands-on, leveraging them to accelerate workflows and increase ambition rather than holding onto old techniques
* Experience with B2B or data-heavy products is a plus, but ability and judgment matter more than years.
## Design Suite
* Strong competence in, or a strong willingness to learn:
* Design & build — Framer (the site is built here)
* Design — Figma
* AI — Claude & Claude Code; ChatGPT & Codex; etc.
## Definition of success
In a year, you're succeeding if:
* You own monitoring, improving, and reporting on the site's performance and technical health, without anyone having to ask
* Website bugs are found and fixed systematically, before they're reported
* Commercial and product requests land with you directly; you prioritise them sensibly, spec them precisely, and ship them reliably
* At least one core section of the website (e.g., Careers; Editorial; Features; Products) is yours end to end, from proposal through to a measured result and ongoing enhancement, both aesthetically and technically
* The site is more consistent across pages, and you can point directly to what you changed
## The Studio Planhat team
The designer-led creative team that defines Planhat's visual identity and storytelling at a standard that sets the company apart in market. We serve GTM and Product as our customers, always optimizing for objective, audience, and constraint, building world-class identity and narrative across every touchpoint.

Recently completed, with a rooftop that opens onto St Pancras and the skyline beyond. The office sits in the Knowledge Quarter at King's Cross — a single square mile home to around a hundred academic, research and commercial institutions, with Google DeepMind, OpenAI and Anthropic among the immediate neighbours. Coal Drops Yard and Granary Square are a few minutes along the canal.
## About us
We're building the operating system for autonomous companies.
The future enterprise is autonomous. Commercial processes that today depend on human effort - servicing, retaining, expanding, selling and supporting — will increasingly be automated. The companies that make this transition will pull ahead. The ones that don't won't survive.
Planhat exists to make that transition real.
We started bootstrapped. Customer-funded, built on discipline instead of venture capital. That foundation shaped everything: how we build, how we sell, how we think about the long game.
Today, Planhat is the agentic customer platform of choice for 700+ companies — powering close to 10 million commercial relationships worldwide and billions of dollars runs through our platform. Wiz, Revolut, Nasdaq, Synthesia, Workday and Dropbox run their customer revenue through Planhat every year.
The shift driving all of this: business is moving to an outcome economy. Companies of the future will not buy software alone anymore — they want outcomes, and they renew or consume more when they get them. That changes everything about what enterprise software needs to be.
The winners will be the ones who build the context layer - a deep, structured, living picture of their business reality. Process automation deployed by operators — not advisors.
The outcome gap is the opportunity. Context is the moat. Deployment is the differentiator. We're building all three.
Our team spans the globe, anchored by offices in Los Angeles, London, and Stockholm. Join us.

You will lead and grow a team of Product Managers, setting direction, raising the bar on craft, and multiplying your impact through them. You will work closely with Engineering, ML, Design, and Customer Success, and play an active role in Encord's enterprise go-to-market motion.
This is a high-autonomy role for someone who is comfortable making independent decisions and driving them through, and who can build a team that does the same.

Encord is the platform the world's most ambitious AI teams use to build them, and you'll be helping define what that platform looks like.
**Hard and Complex Problems:** There is no playbook for what the data layer for AI looks like. You'll be solving novel problems across your product areas: from core platform (tooling that scales from a 10-person startup to a 500-person AV team) to data curation (helping customers turn floods of raw data into high-signal training datasets).
**Ownership and Growth:** Product is represented at the highest levels at Encord. You'll have real ownership: setting strategy, making calls, driving them through, and building the team that executes. As one of the most senior product people in the company, your impact is visible and your trajectory is accelerated.
**What you'll do**

* Manage, coach, and develop Product Managers: setting clear goals, giving regular feedback, reviewing their specs and decisions, and accelerating their growth.

* Lead customer discovery, interviews, problem validation, webinars, and demos, translating complex pain points into clear, winning product bets
* Partner with Sales and Customer Success to drive upsell, cross-sell, and expansion within our largest enterprise accounts
* Collaborate with Engineering and Design to ship high-quality features at pace, writing tight specs, making clear tradeoffs, and holding a high bar for what ships
* Play a leading role in building a high-performing, collaborative product management culture as the team grows
**Experience requirements**
* Experience in product, ideally including time at a rapidly scaling startup. You have seen an organisation scale and know what good product looks like at each stage
* Experience managing or formally mentoring other product managers, or a clear track record of leading through others and a strong desire to step into people management
* Proven experience on B2B SaaS products or technical products sold to enterprise customers. You understand the enterprise sales motion, expansion, and how product decisions connect to revenue
* You speak in metrics and impact, not features shipped. You have worked closely with GTM teams and can tie product decisions to business outcomes
* A self-starter who makes independent decisions and drives them through. You want ownership, not just input. You are energised by ambiguity, not paralysed by it
* You love speaking to customers. You are curious about hard problems at the frontier of AI, and you anticipate needs before customers can fully articulate them
* Excellent communication skills for leading internal sessions and external engagements, customer interviews, demos, and stakeholder presentations
*Encord encourages people from all backgrounds, cultures, and skill levels to apply. You don't need to meet every requirement. We are looking for people who are passionate, customer-focused, and eager to learn.*
**Why Encord**

* Strong in-person culture - most of the team works from our London office 4+ days/week
* 25 days annual leave + UK public holidays
* Annual learning & development budget
* Travel for customer visits, events, and conferences across the UK and Europe
* Company lunches twice a week
* Monthly socials & bi-annual team offsites

## Quant Developer in AI
**You're a quant developer. You've built high-performance systems that process billions of events per day in real-time, and you care deeply about consistency, correctness and performance. Now you want to build in AI**
This is your chance. **Encord is a scale-up serving the frontier of physical AI and robotics, the largest technological revolution in history, where what you build ships fast and you own it.** Help us build the AI data platform for the future of robotics.
## The role
You know how to build systems that are fast and correct under pressure. The hardest problems in AI right now are data problems: distributed, data-intensive systems that have to stay correct and performant at scale.
You will join the Foundations team, who build the data systems that enable frontier robotics labs to generate, understand, train, and test on massive volumes of robotics data. We don’t just react to an order book tick - you will need to handle large 3D scenes, hour-long videos, LIDAR point clouds, and ML inference, all under tight performance and operational budgets.

* Design performant protocols and APIs, and tackle complex domains and immense scale with correct and pragmatic solutions, moving extremely fast while maintaining engineering quality.

You'll begin with a structured induction before joining the Due Diligence team, where you'll work alongside experienced specialists on live client projects.

* Support insurance due diligence projects for private equity firms, investors and corporate clients.
* Research companies, industries and market trends to support transaction activity.
* Analyse information and identify potential risks associated with acquisitions and investments.
* Assist in preparing client reports, presentations and transaction-related deliverables.
* Support colleagues working on live mergers, acquisitions and investment transactions.
* Work closely with clients, legal advisers and internal stakeholders across Howden.
* Develop an understanding of how insurance and risk management support investment decisions and value creation.

**No insurance experience is needed; we’ll teach you everything you need to know!**

* A recent graduate, or in your final year of university study.
* Curious, analytical and motivated to learn.
* Interested in business, financial services, private equity, transactions or consulting.

* Someone who enjoys working with others and building relationships.
* Comfortable analysing information and solving problems.
* Organised and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage competing priorities.
* Resilient and adaptable in a fast-paced environment.
* Someone who takes ownership, shows initiative and enjoys asking questions.
* A collaborative team player who enjoys working across different teams and functions.

At Howden, people are at the heart of everything we do. As an employee-owned business, we believe success is built through collaboration, learning and supporting one another. * Opportunity to complete fully funded professional qualifications, such as the CII or CFA, to support your long-term career development.

* Access to discounted personal health policies, wellbeing support and a range of employee benefits and insurance products.
* 2 days allocated to take part in volunteering schemes.

You'll find resources to help you prepare for our recruitment process and understand which career path could be the best fit for you.

# **What do we offer in return?**
A career that you define. At Howden, we value diversity – there is no one Howden type. Instead, we’re looking for individuals who share the same values as us:
* Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new
* We support each other in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges
* We are determined to make a positive difference at work and beyond
# # **Reasonable adjustments**
We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations at Howden to ensure that our positions align well with your needs. Besides the usual adjustments such as software, IT, and office setups, we can also accommodate other changes such as flexible hours\* or hybrid working\*.
If you're excited by this role but have some doubts about whether it’s the right fit for you, send us your application – if your profile fits the role’s criteria, we will be in touch to assist in helping to get you set up with any reasonable adjustments you may require.

## Company Description
Medicine moves forward here. So will you.
Ergomed is a specialist clinical research organization focused on rare disease and select oncology indications. We focus on the most complex trials, the studies where experience, judgement, and rigorous operational accountability make the biggest difference. We partner with small to midsize biotech companies to move promising therapies through early phase development, so they reach the patients sooner.

Rare disease and oncology trials carry real operational risk, and our people are experts at reducing it, protecting timelines, data quality and the experience of sites and patients at the same time. That is why culture matters to us as much as capability. We have built a collaborative, international team where people share ideas, grow their careers and are trusted to take ownership early. Expedia Group powers travel for everyone, everywhere. As AI becomes core to how travelers plan, book, and manage their trips, it is also changing how we build for them — and merchandising is where that change is furthest along.

We’re Failbetter Games, an award-winning game development studio and makers of *Sunless Sea*, *Sunless Skies*, *Mandrake* and *Fallen London*. We’re known for inventive narrative design, atmospheric storytelling, and rich, fantastical settings.
We’re looking for a Writer and Narrative Designer to join our small in-house team at either a senior or mid level, working specifically on *Fallen London*. This position is permanent, remote, and full time, which for us means 35 hours a week.
We’re based in the United Kingdom, but as long as you can be available during our core hours of 11:00 to 16:00 UK time, you don’t have to be.
Also, if you are based elsewhere, it’s likely we’ll have to structure this as a contract position: we’ve found the administrative requirements for direct employment can be impractical for a studio our size in many jurisdictions.
**About the Role**
You’ll be working on *Fallen London*, an unusual narrative browser game about life in a version of Victorian London that was stolen and installed in a vast underground cavern.
The game is over 16 years old, with more than four and a half million words last time we counted. It’s a live-service RPG we’re actively updating, and very politely free-to-play: development is funded mostly by monthly subscriptions and premium stories. A tabletop roleplaying game in the setting raised over a million dollars on Kickstarter in 2025.
Because we’re a small team, your duties will be varied. You can expect to do all of the following:
* Pitch story arcs to other writers, and take part in high-level planning for the next several months of work.
* Write stories of varying length, complexity, and tone, with a wider range of subject matter than video games usually explore.
* Design quality-based narrative structures that support story and theme while also giving rise to enjoyable gameplay.
* Update and extend existing content (for example, for seasonal events).
* Offer feedback on work by other writers.
* Provide short pieces of marketing copy to explain released or upcoming stories to players – the equivalent of a book’s blurb.
* Draft briefs for artists to help them illustrate your work.
**Requirements**
You don’t need a particular degree or some arbitrary number of shipped titles or years’ experience to work for us. As long as you’re able to do the job well and can demonstrate that in your application, we’d love to hear from you.
Because *Fallen London* is primarily a narrative game and more oriented towards prose than dialogue, we find it benefits from conventional writing skills, of the kind that would be helpful for writing a novel or short story.
Our writing is also denser in choice and consequence than is usual in video games. We use an approach we call quality-based narrative. Qualities, in our parlance, might represent any of the following (and other things besides):
* A character’s capabilities which we can test when the player attempts challenges – for example, how persuasive they are, or their skill with Shapeling Arts.
* Complications and menaces. These might track how scandalised polite society is by a character’s behaviour, or mounting peril on an underground ocean.
* Currencies and resources. These might be physical, like souls in bottles, or abstract, like terrible secrets.
* Aspects of world state that reflect the progress of their current activities, like a complex theft or archaeological expedition.
We're interested in the ways interactivity can produce literary effects, akin to how a writer of conventional fiction might use devices like foreshadowing, metaphor, or just careful choice of syntax or diction. One example we're known for is choices that tempt the player to go against their own character's interests for the sake of humour, emotional catharsis, or plain curiosity.
For this role, we don’t require you to have done previous work with quality-based narrative, but you will need to be comfortable translating your story ideas into this framework. We anticipate that this will usually require you to have experience with some form of interactive writing that goes beyond branching narrative.
Finally, although you don’t need to be a native speaker of English, you will need a very high level of proficiency, including a sensitivity to the nuances of words.
**Optional Extras**
Any of the following would be helpful and worth telling us about in your application, but they’re very much secondary and not required for you to apply:
* Familiarity with *Fallen London* or other games in the same setting.
* System design skills, such as balancing costs and rewards or defining progression curves. (All of *Fallen London*’s game mechanics are also narrative mechanics, so these skills are useful to our writing team.)
* Experience writing functional specs or otherwise clearly explaining desired tooling or game features to programmers.
* Experience guiding freelance writers, from pitching through to completion of a story. (This won’t be part of your initial responsibilities, but many of our monthly Exceptional Stories are written by freelancers, so it could be helpful once you settle into the role.)
**Remote Work**
The entire team is remote, and you don’t have to live in the UK. That said, we’re a British company and pay UK salaries; whether that works in your favour will depend on your location. In particular, this means that our positions are usually not a good fit for residents of the United States, where industry salaries and general cost of living both tend to be much higher.
As mentioned above, we will need you to be available between 11:00 and 16:00 UTC/BST – the way we work benefits too much from real-time communication for us to work asynchronously. How well these hours work for you will usually depend on your own time zone, which accordingly we’ll ask you to tell us as part of the application.
Based on our experience of earlier vacancies, we’d advise that you think carefully before applying if you’re four or more hours removed from the UK. And if you’re six or more hours removed, we’d recommend not applying at all unless there’s something highly unusual about your personal circumstances.
We’re open to sponsoring a UK work visa for this role. If that’s your preference, you are of course welcome to apply regardless of current time zone.
**What We Can Offer**
Failbetter is committed to offering employees a safe, respectful environment, a healthy work-life balance, and transparent decision-making. We strive to avoid crunch and enthusiastically eliminate systemic sources of overtime. We don’t talk over one another in meetings, and we don’t expect all our employees to share the same hobbies and cultural references.
We’ve received a GamesIndustry.biz Best Places to Work award four years out of the last seven, and received their Diversity Award in 2022.
Further benefits of working here include:
* Flexible start times, and strong support for other forms of flexible working, like compressed hours.
* Twenty-five days of leave in addition to UK public holidays.
* Additional leave in every fifth year, as a long service bonus.
* Excellent provisions for parental leave.
* Employer pension contributions.
* Private health insurance.
* Private dental care.
* Reimbursement for annual Covid and flu vaccines.
* Opportunities for paid attendance at industry events.
* An annual, expenses-paid trip to a scenic part of the UK, for our company gathering.
* One silent day a week, to work free of meetings or Slack interruptions.
* Periodic consultations in which we invite subject matter experts to teach us about topics relevant to our work.
If you’re outside the UK and we offer you a contract position, we won’t be able to provide all of these, but we’ll pay you at a higher rate to compensate.
**How to Apply**
If you’d like to be considered for the role, you can apply by completing this single-page form before 9:00 BST on 21 October 2026. The form has nine questions. Most are basic things like name and country of residence. Aside from that, the main things we ask for are:
* A PDF version of your CV.
* One to three short writing samples, at least one must be either prose fiction or from a game (for more details, see the application form and the additional topics section below).
* A cover letter.
**What to Expect After Applying**
You should hear from us within two weeks of the deadline; often, we’re able to reply considerably sooner. We’ll let you know whether or not you make it to the next stage of applications.
We generally invite 5-15% of candidates to that second stage, which involves answering a few short written questions. The third and final stage is a remote interview that usually lasts between 60 and 90 minutes.
#### Additional Topics
**Will you provide feedback on my application?**
If someone completes the second stage of our hiring process, we’re generally able to provide feedback.
Unfortunately, it isn't feasible for us to do so on first-stage applications – we get too many, relative to the size of our team. Also, a lot of the time we'd just be repeating standard advice that's widely available online.
**How long should my writing samples be?**
The length is up to you. However, the shorter the sample, the more likely it is that we'll read the parts that best demonstrate your abilities. It might be better to send us an excerpt with a paragraph of two of context, rather than a full 12 000 word chapter.
**What kinds of samples would be most useful? Are there any you don’t recommend?**
The most useful samples for *Fallen London* tend to be prose fiction, or anything that shows how you’ve used interactivity in your writing. For this reason, we require that at least one sample be prose fiction or from a game.
We generally find it hard to draw useful conclusions from screenplays. Please don’t send us more than one of these.
We won’t generally look at non-fiction samples, as it’s too hard to draw conclusions from them about your preparedness for the role. There are probably some very niche exceptions (if, for example, you made a piece of interactive non-fiction that does something playful or interesting with the player’s input).
**Can I use fan fiction as a sample?**
Yes – we have no prejudices against it. That said, we’d ask that you not send us *Fallen London* fan fiction – paradoxically, that makes certain things harder to judge.
**Should I write a sample tailored specifically to this application?**
We’d advise against it. At this initial stage, we’re looking for general information about your skills as a writer and narrative designer. You don’t need to send us something that matches *Fallen London*’s style, demonstrates detailed knowledge of Victorian England, or otherwise hews particularly close to our existing work.
That said, there probably are situations where it might make sense to write something new – for example, if you’re having trouble picking samples because everything that represents your current abilities is under NDA. But if so, we’d still recommend writing something you expect to be of wider benefit to your portfolio, rather than for this single vacancy.

---

---
#### ABOUT FLIGHTSTORY
We are a media and investment company, and we are on a mission to elevate the stories, build the communities, and support the founders that inspire a happier, healthier humanity. We scale creator-led media, ventures and communities.
---
#### YOUR MISSION
To craft high-performance trailers that scale IP, deepen fandom, and spark global attention through world-class storytelling, platform-native editing, and AI-powered creative intelligence.
As a Trailer Editor at FlightStory, you don’t just cut footage — you engineer attention.
You’ll use performance data to guide creative decisions, AI to accelerate workflows and enhance ideation, and storytelling to convert casual scrollers into lifelong fans. From the first frame to the final export, your edits won’t just look good — they’ll perform every time.
---
#### THE IDEAL CANDIDATE
**Narrative Engineering**
* World-class editorial instincts and understands how to build narrative arcs, emotional payoffs, and retention strategies within short-form edits
* Can turn 90 minutes of footage into 90 seconds of pure story with clarity and rhythm
**Post-Production**
* Fluent in the Adobe suite and complimentary Curious, critical, and confident not just testing AI tools but embedding them into your workflow Experienced across Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, Audition, and Photoshop
**Performance-Driven Creativity**
* Understands and applies data insights from YouTube Studio, TikTok Analytics, and third-party tools (e.g. retention curves, CTR, CVR, audience drop-off)
* Balances gut feel with evidence, knowing when to challenge the data and when to trust it
**Creative Discipline & Ownership**
Takes full ownership of their cut from first assembly to final export
* Thrives in autonomy, executes under pressure, and communicates clearly
**Cross-Functional Collaboration**
* Energised by working with other editors, strategists, social leads, producers, and commercial creatives
* Helps bring everyone into the storytelling process, aligning edit impact with business results
---
#### DAY TO DAY
* You'll read/watch the full recorded episode and take notes of the best moments that could make it into the trailer
* Create a narrative (or script) from the notes that creates a clear and cohesive narrative that also meets the requirements of our Trailer checklist
* Create the sequence, source music, craft the sound design and prepare broll plates for our Animator.
* Work with the trailer team for 1%'s, text, ratios
* Create experimental content to test various elements of the trailer
---
#### YOU’LL THRIVE HERE IF YOU
* Think in story and edit in stats — you love crafting emotionally charged edits, but you also obsess over retention graphs and data-informed structures
* See AI as a creative partner — you’re curious, confident, and hands-on with new tools and find smart ways to integrate them into your workflow
* Believe performance is a craft — you get that storytelling and performance aren’t opposites, they’re allies
* Play for the team — you bring positive energy, contribute ideas, and know how to lift others while staying focused on delivery
* Move like it matters — you’re fast, focused, and clear-headed under pressure; you don’t wait to be told
* Care about the mission — you’re here to build something that moves people and you believe that great editing can change the trajectory of an entire brand
---
#### OUTCOMES
**1. Deliver High-Performance Trailers That Scale Our IP**
Own the full post-production process for trailers and teasers, shaping raw footage into bold, platform-first edits that drive retention, engagement, and cultural relevance
* Build smart, emotionally resonant narratives from interviews, soundbites, music, and motion optimised for YouTube, Reels, and TikTok
* Consistently create trailers that drive clear growth metrics across watch-through rate, shares, average view duration, and subscriber lift
**2. Lead with Data-Informed Storytelling**
* Use performance data to optimise pacing, structure, and creative emphasis
* Collaborate with the Growth and Strategy teams to interpret insights and apply learnings to future edits
* Develop instinct and discipline around which storytelling choices drive performance and back those instincts with evidence
**3. Build and Execute AI-Integrated Editing Workflows**
* Actively use tools like Runway, Descript, ElevenLabs, Fathom, Firefly, or in-house AI
* Drive innovation by testing and refining new AI tools, building systems that make the trailer team faster and smarter
**4. Collaborate and Uplift Team Quality**
* Bring creative direction, references, and smart solutions to brainstorms and edit huddles
* Support junior editors and assistant editors by sharing systems, templates, and AI tools
* Collaborate across creative, social, growth, and commercial teams to deliver trailers that elevate campaigns and IP
