# member of technical staff, biological computing
**frontier** · Cambridge, UK · full-time, permanent founding scientific leadership role (CTO/CSO equivalent) salary: £100,000 to £300,000 (approx. US$135,000 to US$400,000), plus $1–10M in equity
---
## about frontier computing
*frontier computing* works on cultured neural tissue as a computational substrate.
The underlying observation is not new. Biological neurones in vivo perform inference at very low power, several orders of magnitude below what a comparable silicon system would draw, and the cells manufacture themselves.
What has been missing is any serious attempt to find out whether that can be turned into something reproducible, scalable and cheap enough to be useful. For most of the past decade the answer was clearly no, for well understood technical reasons. Several of those reasons have weakened: iPSC differentiation protocols have become more reliable, microfluidic culture systems now survive well past the four week mark, and optimising reading from, and writing into, cultured tissue with multi-electrode arrays is now better understood than ever previously.
We should be plain about where we are. **We have learning on the first scalable substrate, and a strongly supported hypothesis that further buildout of substrate size will bring further computational results, enabling energy efficient computation at scale while circumventing von Neumann architecture bottlenecks.**
That is a starting point, but the significant work ahead is to establish whether the mechanisms we are seeing are reproducible, generalise to more structured circuits, and survive being scaled. Scaling credit assignment is an incredible challenge and an open question within biological neural networks, and one that our company is actively solving.
---
## the research programme
Three codependent problems define the work.
### 1. the cost of culturing substrates at scale
Large scale neuronal culture is currently expensive enough that very few groups can do sustained work with it. We think that is the binding constraint on the whole field, and that it is more tractable than it looks.
The useful denominator is cost per neurone-hour rather than cost per millilitre of media, which decomposes multiplicatively into chemistry, volume and density. Within chemistry the drivers are not where one might expect: in a representative maintenance medium the basal medium and the B-27 supplement together account for the large majority of per-millilitre cost, while the recombinant factors, which are by far the most expensive per milligram, contribute very little because they are dosed at trivial mass. Both of the dominant inputs are commodities, and commodities respond to process work rather than to chemistry.
Volume and density compound on top of chemistry, and have received less attention, largely because the protocols in general use were developed for developmental biology rather than for sustained culture. There is meaningful headroom across the product of the three.
We have made real progress here, and it is the most mature of the three programmes. The goal is not a proprietary advantage in reagent purchasing. It is to bring large scale neuronal culture within reach of ordinary experimental budgets, including our own.
### 2. reproducing core neuronal training mechanisms
Most work in this area imports the reinforcement learning apparatus from silicon: define a global reward, propagate it back, and hope the tissue converges. This is expensive to build and expensive to run, and it scales poorly as neurone count rises and credit assignment gets harder.
We are interested in the opposite approach, which is to let the biology do as much of the learning as it already knows how to do. Local mechanisms, spike-timing dependent plasticity and neuromodulator-gated plasticity among them, are implemented natively by the tissue at no cost to us. If a training environment can be designed so that the desired change is what those mechanisms produce anyway, the control apparatus becomes much simpler and the approach scales with neurone count rather than with the complexity of the reward circuitry.
Our current work is in **cortical computation**, and the near-term direction is to extend it toward **hippocampal circuit work**, where the relationship between architecture, plasticity and function is better characterised and where there is a substantial literature to argue with. The immediate scientific question is whether the learning we see on a simple substrate reproduces in a structured one.
### 3. building out mature neuronal cultures at scale
Culture size is limited by oxygen and nutrient diffusion, and beyond a few millimetres the core of a construct necroses. This is a well known constraint and it is the proximate reason nobody has built a biological system with the connected mass that would make any of this interesting.
Maturation is the second half of the problem and is often treated separately, which we think is a mistake. A large culture of immature neurones is not useful; the target is tissue that is both sizeable and functionally mature, held in that state for the duration of a workload rather than for the duration of an experiment.
Vascularisation is an approach much of the literature takes, and progress there is real. We are already performing our own tissue scaling, and because of this our roadmap is now more closely focused toward culturing more physiologically mature tissue with greater respective computational capacities. We want to hire talent that understands the problem space has moved, and that we are now not only dealing with scale, but also codesigning phenotypic expression with our tissue construct approach to produce *mature* tissue at scale.
---
## about the role
This is the founding scientific leadership position at frontier. We have called it Member of Technical Staff in this job posting rather than Chief Scientific Officer because the substance of the job is closer to running a research group than to running a corporate function: you would set the scientific agenda, choose the problems, build the team, and be accountable for whether the science works. The title officially will be CSO, but your functional work will have much more freedom than this role traditionally implies, given the greenfield nature of the field.
However, your work will fundamentally be application-oriented, designed to push the capacity for biological substrate approaches. This is not a role performing blue-skies research, and the programme will have to be justified towards our business goals. First and foremost, we are looking for someone who understands these tradeoffs, and appreciates that the science they are pursuing must benefit our commercialisation strategy: building larger tissues with both greater and denser computational and memory capacities.
You would be the first senior scientific hire, and as part of that role you will define the future composition of the team alongside the CEO, and help build out a scientific programme that drives substrate progress and feeds into our commercialisation efforts.
### what you would be doing
**Research leadership.** Own the scientific agenda across the three programmes above. Decide what is attacked, in what order, with what resources, and decide what is stopped. Design the experimental programme that takes us from the substrate we have now to something considerably larger, with the network kept in the loop rather than distilled away.
**Building the group.** Recruit and lead the founding scientific team across wet lab, instrumentation and the computational side of the training work. You would have real latitude over who joins and how the group is organised. If you hold views about how research groups ought to be run, this is an unusual opportunity to act on them.
**Technical judgement.** Decisions about tissue configuration, media formulation, electrode interface and training environment interact, and have to be made as a set rather than separately. This is the part of the job that cannot be delegated and is the reason the role exists.
**Scientific representation.** Publish, present, and represent the work to the field, to collaborators, and to the people who need to understand why this is a long horizon programme rather than a short one. Much of the work that you are leading will be kept internal within the short term, while we scale the platform and further our technical moat, but it's vital that we share the fruits of our work with the scientific community as much as can be reasonably permitted.
---
## what we are looking for
A PhD in neuroscience, bioengineering, tissue engineering, biophysics, electrical engineering or a related field, together with a record of independent work: postdoctoral, fellowship-funded, group leader or industrial. We are interested in what you have built and what you understand rather than in how long you have been doing it.
**Substantial hands-on expertise in at least two of the following, and the ability to reason about the whole system:**
* **Neural cell culture.** iPSC differentiation to cortical or other neuronal identities, long duration culture, media formulation, and the practical business of keeping tissue alive and functional over months.
* **In-vitro electrophysiology.** High density and CMOS microelectrode arrays, closed-loop stimulation and recording, spike sorting and population analysis at high channel counts.
* **Tissue engineering and microfluidics.** Three dimensional culture, perfusion, scaffold and substrate design, and a working understanding of designing culture substrates to circumvent the mass transport limits that govern construct size.
* **Computational modelling of neural systems.** Spiking network models, plasticity rules, and the analysis of learning in biological networks.
**We would particularly like to hear from you if you have:**
* Worked on plasticity or learning in cultured or ex-vivo tissue, especially with local rules rather than externally imposed reward. Experience within biocomputing on neural organoids and eliciting learning in these tissues is particularly beneficial.
* A background in hippocampal circuit physiology, or in the relationship between neuronal circuit architecture and memory more generally.
* Taken a biological protocol from research grade to something reproducible and cost controlled, through process development, QC, automation or in-house reagent preparation.
* Worked on maturation or on the size limit in three dimensional neural constructs, and formed a view about it.
* Built instrumentation across electrophysiology, optogenetics, or other related areas — and used it, not only built it.
**A note on temperament, since it matters here as much as technique.** This work suits people who are comfortable being among the few in the world attacking a particular problem, who will stop their own project when the data says to, and who are willing to treat a cost model as a scientific object rather than an administrative chore. It suits people who are not troubled by a thin literature. It is a poor fit for someone who needs an established field to orient within, and we would rather establish that early than late.
We are not looking for someone whose work primarily applies existing organoid culture or MEA tools as instruments. The contribution includes the design of the system itself, recognising the importance of co-development of the technology substrate with the training approach itself.
---
## what we can offer
**Compensation.** £100,000 to £300,000 (approximately US$135,000 to US$400,000 at current rates) depending on experience, plus **$1–10M in equity**, with the vesting schedule to be agreed at offer. The range is genuine and negotiable, and it reflects that this is a founding position. You would be an owner rather than a member of staff.
**Scientific authority.** You choose the problems and you stop the projects. The founder's job is to make sure the company survives long enough for your programme to run. Yours is to make sure it is the right programme to further our technological roadmap.
**Resources.** Recurring biology, wet lab and microfluidics infrastructure are funded, and you would shape what we buy rather than inherit someone else's equipment. Budget for the founding scientific team is yours to allocate. You will not be writing grant applications.
**A decision, promptly.** We will give you an answer within two weeks of a first substantive conversation, and we will tell you the reasoning either way.
**Visa sponsorship.** We can sponsor. Candidates at this level frequently qualify for the UK Global Talent visa, which is quicker and not tied to an employer, and we will support either route and cover the costs.
**The right to publish.** You will publish. Where something is commercially sensitive we will say so and agree a timeline with you in advance. Protecting your scientific standing is a condition of this working, not a concession we are making. With regard to that, much of the biocomputing work will likely be limited to being published after a 2 year period, particularly regarding core IP that generates value for the company. We will however ensure that you have time to work on problems that lean towards basic science and will be significant contributions within neuroscience, and you will be resourced financially and empowered in hiring decisions to be able to do this.
**Location.** UK based, in the lab. This is wet work and cannot be done remotely. We are open to discussing relocation, but your role will require you to be physically located in Cambridge with the rest of the team that we will be hiring.
### please read this before applying
*frontier computing* has raised **$10M+ to date**, and is actively raising more. That provides genuine runway and a substantial equipment budget, which in practice means the research programme you design is one you would get to run rather than one you spend a year fundraising against.
The team at present is the founder, Michael Domarkas: Cambridge physicist, four years in neuromorphic computing and two of those specifically on organoid computation, and has been grant funded to work on this previously. You would be joining a funded company with a small number of serious competitors worldwide and almost no organisational inheritance. Depending on your temperament it is either the most appealing or the most uncomfortable thing about the position.
We have tried to describe the state of the science accurately rather than favourably. If the risk profile is wrong for you at this point in your career, we would rather know now than half way through your first year in the company. We'd still be interested in chatting with you, particularly around roles that might become relevant in the future.
---
## how to apply
Please send the following to hiring@frontier.site, with **"MTS application, [your surname]"** in the subject line.
1. **A CV**, in whatever format you prefer. Include publications that are published and accessible, with links; nothing in preparation. Include funding you have held, making clear what was awarded to you personally as against a consortium, and anyone you have supervised.
2. **A research statement, maximum three pages.** Describe the three pieces of work you consider most important, with links, and what they established. Then describe what you would do here: which of the three problems you would take first, what you would need, and what evidence within twelve months would tell you that you were wrong.
3. **A one page letter** on why this rather than the alternatives available to you. We want to hear what excites you about doing science with us, and what motivates you in our research and engineering mission.
4. **Thoughts on team**, any postdocs that you would want to bring on to work with you, and how you think about working with a team that is diverse across age and technical backgrounds, understanding that significant portions of the team buildout will be under our engineering roles to empower scaling the work you will have helped develop.

“CVI Infrared Optics is a part of the IDEX Materials, Science and Solutions (MSS) platform. Besides our unique capabilities in manufacturing large optics from visible to longwave, we are backed by the combined capabilities of our platform. CVI offers a full spectrum of optical engineering, manufacturing, and assembly expertise. Together we can support all our customers with more engineering expertise, broader capabilities, and extensive manufacturing resources. Since 1982, CVI Infrared Optics has been manufacturing advanced optical components for high performance optronics systems. We have become the leading experts in manufacturing and integration of large optics from visible, and near infrared, to longwave infrared, that can continuously perform in extreme weather climates and harsh conditions.
When you need robust optical components and assembly expertise for your mission critical application, we can provide world-class solutions.“
**About the Role**
We are seeking a highly skilled **Thin Film Coating Engineer** to join our growing engineering team. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in the development, optimisation, and production of advanced thin film coatings used in high-performance optical, electrical, and mechanical applications.
Working closely with R&D, Manufacturing, Quality, and Engineering teams, you will be responsible for developing robust coating processes, improving product quality, supporting production scale-up activities, and ensuring coatings consistently meet demanding customer specifications.
If you have a passion for vacuum coating technologies, process improvement, and solving complex manufacturing challenges, we'd love to hear from you.
**Key Responsibilities**
**Process Development & Optimisation**
* Design and develop thin film coating stacks using modelling and simulation software such as Essential Macleod, TFCalc, or OptiLayer.
* Develop and optimise deposition processes using technologies including PVD (sputtering and e-beam evaporation) and/or CVD.
* Plan and execute Design of Experiments (DOE) to establish robust process windows and improve process capability.
* Support the transition of new coating designs from development into high-volume production.
* Scale coating processes while maintaining performance, yield, and repeatability.
**Quality & Continuous Improvement**
* Establish and maintain Statistical Process Control (SPC) systems for key coating parameters.
* Define and maintain quality standards for raw materials, in-process inspections, and finished products.
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives using Lean and problem-solving methodologies to reduce defects and improve yields.
* Support non-conformance investigations, Root Cause Analysis, CAPA activities, and Material Review Board (MRB) processes.
* Ensure compliance with quality standards and management systems, including ISO 9001.
**Testing & Characterisation**
* Analyse coating performance using spectrophotometers and other metrology equipment.
* Support calibration, Gauge R&R studies, and maintenance of coating measurement systems.
* Design and oversee environmental and reliability testing, including thermal cycling, humidity, adhesion, and durability assessments.
* Verify coating performance against customer drawings and specifications.
**Equipment & Manufacturing Support**
* Support the operation, maintenance, and optimisation of vacuum deposition systems.
* Troubleshoot coating equipment, vacuum systems, and process-related issues.
* Develop and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
* Train and mentor technicians and operators on coating processes and best practices.
**Leadership & Collaboration**
* Provide technical leadership and guidance to technicians and engineers.
* Work collaboratively across Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, and R&D teams.
* Participate in regular production and quality reviews to drive improvements in productivity and quality.
* Build strong working relationships with customers, suppliers, and external partners.
**Health, Safety & Compliance**
* Follow the site's comprehensive safety regulations, promptly report any risks, hazards or incidents, and ensure a safe workplace by adhering to all established protocols.
* Support company values, ethical conduct and integrity in all activities.
**What We're Looking For**
**Essential Qualifications & Experience**
* Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Materials Science, Physics, Chemical Engineering, or a related STEM discipline.
* Minimum 5 years' experience working with industrial vacuum deposition systems.
* Proven experience developing and optimising thin film coating processes in a manufacturing environment.
* Strong understanding of coating metrology, process characterisation, and quality systems.
* Experience with statistical process control, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Ability to interpret engineering drawings and technical specifications.
* Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
**Desirable**
* Experience within a high-volume manufacturing environment.
* Experience working directly with customers and suppliers.
* Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing principles.
* Understanding of ISO 14001 and Health & Safety requirements.
* Membership of a relevant professional engineering institution.
**Why Join Us?**
* Opportunity to work on cutting-edge coating technologies and advanced manufacturing processes
* Competitive salary
* Annual bonus scheme
* 25 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays
* Company pension scheme
* Healthcare benefits
* On-site employee benefits
* Opportunities for professional development and career progression

Our job is to find where those journeys break, prove what the breakage costs, and drive the fix through to a measured result.

You work out where friction and servicing demand are really coming from, build the evidence for what will remove them, and drive those changes through to delivery and proven results. Working directly alongside the Head of Journey Transformation in a small core team, you will help establish our journey intelligence capability from the ground up: the mapping standards, the diagnostic methods and the evidence bar the team is held to.
* Change runs down two routes. Some is delivered directly within Operations, through our servicing and contact centre technology estate - and you will own that end to end. Some belongs on the roadmaps of other teams, such as app and web product, platform APIs, marketing or compliance, and has to earn its place there on the strength of the evidence behind it - so you will build cases strong enough to do that, then carry them through the governance that prioritises them.

By the end of year one:
* A credible current-state picture exists across our priority journeys, client and operational, to a standard the business trusts and returns to.
* Journey improvement runs as an ongoing cycle rather than a series of projects: a pipeline that always holds the next evidenced opportunity and shipped changes that continue to be optimised against live performance.

# Why Isio?
Starting your career is about more than finding a job. It's about finding a place where you can learn, grow and make an impact.

# Defined Contribution Pensions Investment Advisory
Our **Defined Contribution (DC) Pensions Investment Advisory team** helps employers and trustees make informed investment decisions for workplace pension schemes. The team sits within Isio’s wider **Employee Benefits** business, where we help clients design, manage and improve the benefits they offer to their people.
As a Graduate Analyst, you’ll support client work that helps pension schemes run effectively and deliver better outcomes for members. You’ll build your knowledge of pensions, investment strategy, financial markets and DC providers while studying for a relevant professional qualification.
You do not need to have studied pensions or investment before. We’ll support you to build the technical knowledge, professional skills and confidence you need to develop your career.
# What does the role entail?
* Preparing DC pensions investment performance reports for clients
* Drafting investment reports on fund selection, default strategy reviews and DC investment projects
* Researching pension providers, investment managers and investment products
* Supporting provider reviews, including analysing tender responses and summarising findings
* Building financial models to help clients understand investment risks and expected returns
* Monitoring how client investment strategies are performing against their objectives
* Supporting work on capital markets views and investment opportunities
* Helping clients implement investment advice efficiently
* Responding to provider and client queries by email and phone, with support from your team
* Sharing knowledge and working collaboratively with colleagues across the department
You’ll also learn how our wider Employee Benefits business supports clients across benefit design, benefits technology, risk and healthcare broking, pensions, workplace savings advice, governance and employee support.

We’re looking for people who are curious, analytical and motivated to learn. You’ll need to be comfortable working with numbers and interested in financial markets, investment or long-term savings.
* You’ll be suited to this role if you enjoy:
* Solving problems and working with data
* Learning technical concepts and applying them to real client work
* Explaining information clearly to different audiences
* Working with others to deliver high-quality outcomes
* Managing your time and balancing different priorities
* Building confidence in a client-facing environment over time

As a DC Pensions Investment Advisory Graduate Analyst, you’ll study for the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) exams or an equivalent qualification.
We recognise the commitment involved in balancing work and study, so you’ll be supported with study leave and tutorials. You’ll also receive:
* A induction where you’ll meet peers and senior leaders
* Technical training to help you build pensions and investment knowledge
* Support to develop professional and consulting skills
* A buddy from your first day to help you settle in
* Study Mentor to guide you through your study and exam journey
* Performance Manager to support your development and progress
* Opportunities to build wider market knowledge throughout your career
# Length of training:
Around 3 years to achieve your relevant professional qualification, however you are employed on a permanent basis from the start of your graduate role.
# Location and working pattern
This role is based in our **Edinburgh** office.
Expected office attendance, including the first few months is four days per week minimum in office and then two/three days a week in the office moving forwards.
The working pattern will reflect client, team and learning needs. Reasonable adjustments will be considered where appropriate.
# Entry requirements:
* You must have completed an undergraduate degree or higher-level qualification by 20 September 2027 and achieved a 2.1 or higher. If you are in your final year, you should be on track to achieve this
* We welcome applications from people studying any subject
* You will need an interest in data, technology and business problem-solving
We are not able to provide visa sponsorship for this position and therefore you will need to be able to work in the UK without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future.
**Start date:** 22 September 2027
# Recruitment process
The recruitment process will include;
* completing an online application form where we will establish your eligibility for this role
* an invitation to complete a ‘Skills that Build’ assessment and numerical reasoning online assessment - more information on this is available here
* online motivation and competency questions requiring video and/or written responses
* review of your application assessing your potential to be successful in this role
* an interview, in-person, with Managers in this role in the office you have applied to be based in
We will explain what to expect before each stage. The process will assess your motivation, numerical and problem-solving skills, communication, teamwork and approach to learning. It will not assume previous pensions knowledge.
# What you can expect in return
* A competitive salary and a market-leading bonus scheme, with stretch targets to reward high performance
* Study support to help you achieve professional qualifications, with salary increases for exam passes
* Development and training opportunities to support your career ambitions throughout your time with us
* A friendly and supportive team who will help you deliver your best work

Click ‘Apply’ and follow the simple online application process.

# Country Intelligence Lead Analyst - Latin America
Croydon, England, United Kingdom
Janes empowers military, government, and defense leaders to act with confidence in an increasingly complex world. Our trusted defense, security, and geopolitical information delivered through seamless digital platforms and system integrations—turns overwhelming data into clear, actionable intelligence and insight. By filling critical information gaps, Janes helps customers analyze threats, accelerate decisions, and stay ahead of emerging challenges.
**Job purpose:** The Lead Analyst will lead the Country Intelligence **Latin America** desk, managing and developing a team of analysts responsible for OSINT intelligence coverage across the region. This is a senior analytical and client-facing role requiring extensive knowledge of Mexican Non-State and Armed Groups (NSAGs) and Serious and Organised Crime data as well as a strong understanding of the wider Latin American security and geopolitical environment.
The successful candidate will be a recognised Mexico specialist, fluent in Spanish, and have a well-developed network of regional contacts and sources. They will bring considerable proven experience from a comparable intelligence, security, defence, government, risk or research environment and be able to engage with senior clients and stakeholders.
The position will also have a strong focus on the evolving US–Mexico security relationship and the strategic importance of Mexico within the wider Americas. Relevant issues include organised crime and cartel activity, narcotics trafficking, security cooperation, political and institutional stability, and changes in US and Mexican policy that may affect the regional security environment.
The Lead Analyst will drive the maintenance and enhancement of foundational country intelligence, including Political, Military, Economic, Social, Information and Infrastructure (PMESII) assessments, CBN coverage, NSAG profiles, and serious and organised crime content. They will monitor developments, commission and produce analysis, review the work of their team, and deliver written assessments in accordance with Janes' rigorous analytical standards.
As a senior subject-matter expert, the successful candidate will also represent Janes with customers and other external stakeholders.
The Country Intelligence Lead Analyst - Latin America – Latin America will report to the Principal Analyst, Latin America, NATO and Europe.
**How you will contribute at Janes:** * Lead Janes' open-source intelligence research and analysis on national security, geopolitical and stability risks across Latin America, with particular responsibility for Mexico.
* Serve as a senior subject-matter expert on Mexico, with particular expertise in NSAGs, cartels, serious and organised crime, security institutions and the political-security environment.
* Maintain and expand a trusted network of relevant regional contacts and sources to strengthen Janes' understanding of developments in Mexico and Latin America.
* Lead the updating and enhancement of foundational intelligence products, ensuring coverage reflects current intelligence priorities, emerging threats and changes in the regional security environment.
* Manage, mentor and develop analysts, setting research priorities, allocating work and ensuring consistently high analytical and editorial standards.
* Review and quality-assure analytical output, challenging assumptions and ensuring assessments are evidence-based, appropriately sourced and clearly communicate confidence and uncertainty.
* Identify intelligence gaps and emerging issues requiring additional collection or analytical attention.
* Produce timely written assessments, short-form and longer-form analytical content for senior decision-makers and stakeholders.
* Deliver authoritative briefings to clients and respond confidently to questions from government, defence, security and commercial audiences.
* Build relationships with customers and internal stakeholders, using their intelligence requirements and feedback to help shape research priorities and product development.
* Contribute to the continued development of analytical methodologies, structured analytical techniques and best practices across the Country Intelligence team.
**The ideal skills and experience for this role are:** * Specialist expertise relating to Mexico, demonstrated through substantial professional experience researching or working on Mexican political, security, defence, intelligence or organised crime issues.
* Fluent Spanish and English, including the ability to conduct advanced research using Spanish-language primary and secondary sources and engage professionally with Spanish-speaking contacts and stakeholders.
* An established and relevant network of contacts in Mexico and/or the wider region, potentially spanning government, security, defence, academia, journalism, civil society and specialist research communities.
* Detailed knowledge of Mexican NSAGs, cartels and serious and organised crime, including their organisational structures, leadership, geographic presence, capabilities, revenue streams, alliances and competition.
* Strong knowledge of wider Latin American security, political and geopolitical dynamics and an ability to place developments in Mexico within their regional and international context.
* Considerable proven experience in a comparable intelligence, defence, national security, political risk, geopolitical analysis or specialist research role.
* Proven experience leading analysts or researchers, setting priorities, managing workflows and developing colleagues.
* Excellent OSINT collection and analytical skills, with the ability to identify, validate and interpret information from complex and sometimes contradictory source environments.
* Strong source evaluation skills and an understanding of the particular challenges associated with researching organised crime and security issues in Mexico.
* Proven experience in intelligence assessment, risk assessment, scenario analysis and the production of concise, decision-relevant intelligence reporting.
* Strong critical-thinking skills and the ability to distinguish reporting from assessment, identify intelligence gaps, challenge assumptions and communicate analytical confidence and uncertainty.
* Excellent briefing and presentation skills, with demonstrable experience communicating complex intelligence assessments to senior audiences and responding authoritatively to questions.
* Excellent written English, editorial judgement and attention to detail, with the ability to review and improve the analytical work of others.
* Strong stakeholder and client-management skills and the confidence to represent Janes externally as a senior subject-matter expert.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality intelligence content to deadline.
* Strong data analysis skills together with advanced online and electronic research capabilities.

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

What will I be doing?
Kaluza runs the billing and payments engine behind some of the world's biggest energy retailers. Every bill sent and every payment collected across Kaluza's markets increasingly runs through one shared core platform, and GBPA exists to build and run that core, so foundational billing and payments capability gets built once and reused everywhere, rather than rebuilt separately for every new market or client relationship.
That matters because of where Kaluza is headed: as we grow into new markets and take on more of the world's largest energy retailers as clients, rebuilding core billing and payments capability separately for each one is slower, costlier, and more error-prone than building it once and configuring it at the edge. Getting this right directly shapes how fast Kaluza can bring new markets and clients onto the platform, and how reliable that platform is once they're on it.
We're also in the middle of reorganising how this part of the business works, moving from building billing and payments capability separately per area toward one shared global core that every area configures rather than rebuilds. You'll lead engineering across two GBPA domains through complex, ambiguous, cross-squad initiatives.
You'll own technical and product strategy across both domains simultaneously, rather than handing strategy off to a single team.
You'll diagnose systemic and organisational issues using deep domain knowledge, not just resolve team-level technical problems.
You'll manage cross-functional stakeholders across Product, Delivery, and adjacent engineering teams to align roadmap and trade-offs.

You'll operate in a high-integrity data domain (billing and payments) where reliability and reconciliation come before speed.

Have a track record of successfully navigating complex stakeholder and leadership dynamics, influencing the wider organisation beyond your direct scope to improve product quality and team experience.

Experience mentoring senior engineers toward people-leadership roles.

**Group Financial Controller**
**Location: Exeter or Truro (Hybrid working)**

**Salary: Competitive + Benefits**

At Kensa, we’re making heating better - for people, for the planet and for the future. Since 1999, we’ve been leading the way in ground source heat pump technology, delivering affordable, low-carbon heating solutions that support the UK’s transition to net zero.
We’re looking for a Group Financial Controller to lead financial control, reporting, compliance and accounting across the Kensa Group. This is a senior, influential role at the heart of our Finance function, providing the robust governance and high-quality information we need to grow sustainably.
If you’re a qualified finance professional with strong technical accounting knowledge, experience of group reporting and a track record of developing high-performing teams, this could be an opportunity to make a visible impact in a growing, purpose-driven business.
**The role**
As Group Financial Controller, you’ll lead the Group’s month-end and year-end close, consolidated financial reporting, statutory compliance and audit activity. You’ll oversee transactional finance, balance sheet control, cash management and treasury processes, ensuring accurate, timely and audit-ready information across all entities.
You’ll work closely with the Finance Director, FP&A, Commercial Finance and Leadership teams, translating complex financial information into clear insight while maintaining the controls, systems and processes that underpin effective decision-making. You’ll also lead and develop the finance team, creating clarity, accountability and opportunities for growth.
**What you’ll be doing**
* Leading the Group’s month-end and year-end close processes, ensuring accurate and timely results
* Overseeing consolidated financial statements and reporting in line with relevant accounting standards
* Maintaining and continuously improving financial policies, procedures and internal control frameworks
* Ensuring compliance with statutory requirements, tax obligations and external audit processes
* Managing relationships with external auditors and coordinating audit work across all entities
* Overseeing accounts payable, accounts receivable, banking, payroll interfaces and the general ledger
* Maintaining robust balance sheet controls, reconciliations and audit-ready documentation
* Strengthening cash management, cash flow reporting and treasury processes
* Providing technical accounting support and clear financial insight to operational teams and senior leaders
* Partnering with FP&A to align actuals, forecasts and business performance
* Supporting the financial aspects of major projects, investments and strategic initiatives
* Leading, coaching and developing the finance team, with clear expectations and effective performance management
* Identifying opportunities to automate, streamline and standardise finance processes across the Group
* Improving the integration of financial and operational systems as Kensa continues to scale
**What we’re looking for**
You’ll be a credible and collaborative finance leader who combines strong technical knowledge with a practical, improvement-focused approach. You’ll be comfortable operating at both strategic and detailed levels, managing competing deadlines and communicating clearly with stakeholders across the organisation.
Skills and experience:
* Professional accounting qualification - ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent
* Proven experience in a senior financial control or group accounting role, ideally within a multi-entity or fast-growing organisation
* Strong technical accounting knowledge and experience preparing consolidated group financial statements
* Experience managing audits, statutory reporting and compliance requirements
* Demonstrable leadership experience, with the ability to develop and manage a high-performing finance team
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with excellent attention to detail

We are looking for an experienced contractor to lead the analysis, design and execution of a data migration from one Salesforce instance (source org) to another (target org), using Microsoft SQL Server as the staging and transformation layer. You will own the end-to-end migration data workstream: profiling source data, mapping objects and fields, building transformation logic, loading and reconciling data, and supporting cutover.
This is a hands-on, delivery-focused role. The right person will combine strong Salesforce data model knowledge with proven, real-world experience of moving data between orgs safely and accurately. Define and document the data migration approach, scope, and sequencing for moving data between Salesforce orgs, including cutover and rollback considerations.
Analyse and profile source Salesforce data to assess volumes, quality, duplication, and dependencies across standard and custom objects.
Produce object-level and field-level mapping documents between source and target orgs, covering data types, picklist values, record types, required fields, and validation rules.
Design and maintain SQL Server staging databases and schemas to extract, cleanse, transform, and stage Salesforce data ahead of loading.
Write, optimise, and test T-SQL (stored procedures, views, ETL logic) to implement transformation and data-cleansing rules.
Manage the migration of parent/child relationships and record ownership, preserving referential integrity through ID cross-referencing (source ID to target ID) and correct load order.

Strong SQL Server and T-SQL skills, including stored procedures, joins across large data sets, performance tuning, and data quality checks.

We are looking for an experienced contractor to lead the analysis, design and execution of a data migration from one Salesforce instance (source org) to another (target org), using Microsoft SQL Server as the staging and transformation layer. You will own the end-to-end migration data workstream: profiling source data, mapping objects and fields, building transformation logic, loading and reconciling data, and supporting cutover.
This is a hands-on, delivery-focused role. The right person will combine strong Salesforce data model knowledge with proven, real-world experience of moving data between orgs safely and accurately. The role can be filled at Data Analyst or Data Architect level depending on the candidate’s experience; architect-level candidates will additionally be expected to shape the overall migration approach and standards.
\n
Main Duties / Responsibilities:
Define and document the data migration approach, scope, and sequencing for moving data between Salesforce orgs, including cutover and rollback considerations.
Analyse and profile source Salesforce data to assess volumes, quality, duplication, and dependencies across standard and custom objects.
Produce object-level and field-level mapping documents between source and target orgs, covering data types, picklist values, record types, required fields, and validation rules.
Design and maintain SQL Server staging databases and schemas to extract, cleanse, transform, and stage Salesforce data ahead of loading.
Write, optimise, and test T-SQL (stored procedures, views, ETL logic) to implement transformation and data-cleansing rules.
Manage the migration of parent/child relationships and record ownership, preserving referential integrity through ID cross-referencing (source ID to target ID) and correct load order.
Extract and load data using appropriate tooling (e.g., Salesforce Data Loader, Bulk API, SSIS, Azure Data Factory, dbAmp, or equivalent) and manage error handling and re-runs.
Plan and run multiple migration cycles (development, test/UAT, and production dress rehearsals) and execute the production cutover.
Design and run reconciliation and validation checks (record counts, field-level comparisons, sampling) and produce sign-off evidence for business stakeholders.
Work with Salesforce administrators, developers, business analysts, and data owners to resolve data quality issues and agree transformation rules.
Identify and manage migration risks and issues, including data volume limits, API limits, automation and trigger impacts, and sharing/ownership considerations.
Ensure the handling of personal data complies with GDPR and internal data governance and security standards.
Produce clear documentation and a handover pack (mapping specifications, scripts, runbooks, lessons learned) so the migration can be supported after your engagement ends.
Essential Skills & Qualifications:
Proven, hands-on experience delivering data migrations between Salesforce orgs or from other systems into Salesforce, ideally including at least one full production cutover.
Strong working knowledge of the Salesforce data model, including standard objects (e.g., Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, Case, User) and custom objects, relationships (lookup and master-detail), record types, and field types.
Strong SQL Server and T-SQL skills, including stored procedures, joins across large data sets, performance tuning, and data quality checks.
Experience with data extraction and loading tools for Salesforce (e.g., Data Loader, Bulk API, SSIS, Azure Data Factory, Informatica, Talend, Boomi, dbAmp, or similar).
Solid experience in data profiling, cleansing, deduplication, and mapping, with a methodical approach to reconciliation and audit trails.
Understanding of Salesforce migration considerations such as ownership and sharing, validation rules, triggers/flows, API limits, and managing record IDs across orgs.
Awareness of data privacy requirements (e.g., GDPR) and secure handling of customer data.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate technical data concepts for business stakeholders and to work independently in a fast-paced delivery environment.
Desirable skillsets:
Salesforce certifications (e.g., Salesforce Certified Data Architecture and Management Designer, Administrator, or Platform App Builder).
Experience with multi-org consolidation or Salesforce org merge/split projects.
Experience with Salesforce Sales Cloud and/or Service Cloud in an automotive or retail environment.
Familiarity with Salesforce attachments, files, and content migration (ContentVersion, ContentDocumentLink).
Experience using Power BI or similar tools to present reconciliation and migration progress reporting.
Working knowledge of Agile delivery and tools such as Jira and Confluence.

* Utilities and energy: electricity, gas, water, heat networks and standby power, together with resilience planning and energy performance.
* Planned and reactive maintenance, asset management, lifecycle and backlog maintenance planning.
* Statutory and regulatory compliance across the estate, including fire, water hygiene, gas, electrical, asbestos, lifts and pressure systems.
* Minor works and small capital projects delivered through the operations team, technical input to major capital schemes, and the operational interfaces with security, cleaning, grounds and logistics services.
* Provide senior technical and operational leadership, setting priorities and standards for a multi-disciplinary in-house team and outsourced service partners.
* Support statutory compliance and health and safety performance for the operational estate, including governance, reporting, audit response and remediation of findings.
* Manage operational budgets running to several million pounds, including maintenance, utilities and minor works, and drive value for money from contracts and suppliers.
* Guide the management of hard FM and specialist contracts, including performance management, variations and re-procurement where required, and maintain resilience and business continuity for critical infrastructure, including incident response and out-of-hours escalation.
* Provide technical assurance to capital projects and estates strategy, including design reviews, commissioning and handover, and support the client’s carbon reduction and energy performance objectives.
* Build effective working relationships with academic departments, professional services, students’ representatives and external stakeholders, and represent the estates function at senior governance forums.
* Ensure a smooth handover on completion of the assignment, leaving clear documentation, plans and priorities for the permanent post-holder.
About you:

**Essential**
* Substantial senior leadership experience in estates or campus operations for a large, complex organisation, ideally in higher education, healthcare, research or another 24/7 public-facing environment.
* A strong engineering or building services background, with a degree or equivalent and chartered status or equivalent professional standing (for example CIBSE, IET, IMechE, RICS or IWFM).
* Demonstrable ownership of statutory compliance and health and safety across a large estate, with a working knowledge of the relevant UK regulations and guidance.
* Experience managing multi-million-pound operational budgets and large hard FM or engineering contracts.
* Track record of leading in-house teams and outsourced service partners through periods of change.
* Credibility with senior executives and academic stakeholders, with clear, concise written and verbal communication.

**Desirable**
* Experience within a university or research-intensive environment, including laboratory and specialist facilities.
* Experience of interim or transition roles, including stabilising teams and handing over to a permanent appointee.

Interim technical appointments are often about holding the line until a permanent post-holder arrives. This one is not. You bring the seniority and take the decisions; we make sure you are not the only person carrying them.

GMG Governance & Operating Model

Manage and refine the Data Management Operating Model for GMG and its contracts. Align it to the organisational strategy and DHSC contractual rules, focusing on the BI Hub.
Define and monitor governance benchmarks, maturity measures, and compliance reporting.
Serve as the BI Hub authority on Data Governance, Information Security and Compliance.
Data Security & Risk Management
Guide the application of security-by-design principles across BI Hub platforms and services as well as other platforms employed throughout the business unit.
Ensure adherence to UK GDPR, Data Protection Act, Cyber Essentials, NHS Data Security and Protection requirements, and relevant government standards.
Perform data risk evaluations and assist with Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) and Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) for the BI Hub and all other GMG platforms.
Lead remediation efforts for identified governance, security, and compliance risks across the BI Hub and broader GMG services.
Collaborate with Information Governance and DDaT teams to ensure secure data architecture and access controls.
Data Quality & Metadata Management
Define company-wide criteria for data quality, metadata oversight, and master data administration.
Carry out data quality monitoring and assurance procedures across BI Hub datasets and broader GMG data assets.
Develop and sustain business glossaries, data catalogues, and data lineage documentation.
Ensure data quality issues are identified, prioritised and resolved through appropriate governance processes.
Regulatory Compliance & Information Management
Ensure all GMG activities and contractual obligations stay aligned with legislative and regulatory requirements, prioritising the BI Hub.
Support audits, assurance reviews and external assessments.
Advise collaborators on data governance and information management guidelines.
AI & New Technologies Governance
Develop governance structures for analytics, automation, and AI solutions provided through the BI Hub and wider GMG initiatives.
Establish controls for ethical use of AI, model oversight, and responsible innovation.
Support risk assessment and assurance activities for advanced analytics and machine learning initiatives.

Job Title: Information Security Project Manager
Reports to: Director of Technical Operations Location: UK / Estonia / US (remote-friendly within these regions)
Role purpose
The Information Security Project Manager is responsible for coordinating and driving the company’s information security activities in a pragmatic, commercially aware way. This role exists to manage security-related projects, audits, and customer security interactions so that we stay compliant and credible without blocking sensible business decisions or over-engineering controls.
Scope and context
This role sits within the technology function and partners closely with Technical Operations, Engineering, Product, Legal, and Sales. The focus is on governance, coordination, and communication, not on dictating policy in isolation or acting as the final decision-maker on security matters. Final risk and tooling decisions sit with the Director of Technical Operations and the broader leadership team; the Information Security Project Manager’s job is to provide clear input, well-reasoned recommendations, and organised execution.
We are a growing SaaS business without PCI, PHI, or highly sensitive PII in scope, and we are not subject to HIPAA or classified/secret information regime – our security approach should be proportionate: strong, credible, and well-documented, but not theatrical or unnecessarily restrictive.
Key responsibilities
ISO 27001 and internal audits
* Plan, coordinate, and execute internal audits and control reviews against ISO 27001 (and related frameworks where relevant).
* Maintain audit schedules, evidence repositories, and action logs so that we are consistently “audit ready” rather than scrambling before assessments.
* Work with control owners across the business to ensure that required processes are in place, understood, and operating in a pragmatic way.
* Track findings and remediation actions, ensuring owners are clear on what needs to be done and by when, and following up to completion.
* Support external ISO 27001 surveillance and recertification audits, including planning, evidence collation, and managing auditor queries.
Security projects and initiatives
* Coordinate discrete security improvement projects (for example, rolling out new security tooling, tightening access controls, or updating key policies).
* Break down security initiatives into clear tasks, owners, and timelines, and keep stakeholders informed on progress and risks.
* Work with Technical Operations and Engineering to ensure technical changes are understood, documented, and reflected in our security posture.
* Help prioritise security work by articulating risk, impact, and effort, while understanding the wider commercial and delivery context.
Customer security, RFPs and RFQs
* Partner with Sales, Pre-Sales, and Customer Success to respond to customer security questionnaires, RFPs, RFQs, and due diligence requests.
* Maintain and continuously improve a central library of standard security responses and artefacts (for example, summaries of our controls, certifications, and processes).
* Coordinate input from Technical Operations, Engineering, and Legal where deeper technical or contractual responses are required.
* Attend customer calls when needed to explain our security posture in clear, non-alarmist language and build confidence in our approach.
Security information and communication
* Develop and maintain a clear, concise view of our security posture that can be communicated internally and to customers (for example, how we handle data, access, monitoring, and incident response at a high level).
* Ensure that key facts (such as use of encryption at rest and in transit, SSO capabilities, backup approaches, and incident processes) are understood and kept up to date, even if technical details are owned by others.
* Translate technical explanations from engineers into language suitable for non-technical audiences, including customers and internal stakeholders.
* Help ensure that security-related messages are proportionate, avoiding both complacency and unnecessary drama.
Policies, standards, and pragmatic governance
* Maintain a focused, manageable set of security policies and procedures that reflect how we actually operate.
* Work with policy owners to keep documents current, usable, and aligned to ISO 27001 and customer expectations, avoiding policy sprawl and unnecessary complexity.
* Coordinate periodic reviews of key policies and standards, ensuring changes are communicated and understood.
* Provide recommendations to the Director of Technical Operations on improvements to policies, controls, or tooling, with clear reasoning and trade-offs.
What this role is not
* This is not a “head of security” or ultimate decision-maker role; final go/no-go and tooling decisions sit with the Director of Technical Operations and leadership.
* This is not a role for writing endless policies or blocking change; it is about enabling sensible decisions with good information and structured follow-through.

### We are looking for a Senior Associate specialising in Group Tax for our Tax and Reward group.
## About Macfarlanes
Macfarlanes is a pre-eminent law firm that serves a global client base in Private Capital, Private Wealth, M&A and Disputes. Personal connection, an entrepreneurial spirit and a commitment to excellence are at the heart of our firm. These values drive our ability to deliver exceptional outcomes for our clients.

Our culture is challenging and supportive, creating an environment where individuals can thrive.

As an experienced Associate, you will focus on sophisticated, hands-on client advisory work within a collaborative, Partner-led team. You will run matters with genuine autonomy, work at the heart of complex client engagements and help deliver high-quality advice as part of a team that uniquely combines corporate tax and private client expertise. Macfarlanes is the only UK firm ranked Band 1 by Chambers for both corporate tax and private client tax.
You will work alongside Partners and colleagues who value technical excellence, and your work will be recognised for its quality and depth. You will be trusted to manage and deliver on complex matters, building strong relationships with clients and colleagues while playing a substantive role in delivering practical, high-quality advice.
A significant proportion of our work involves advising UK and international privately owned groups on cross-border structuring, multi-jurisdictional tax risk management and international tax developments. This is sophisticated, multi-jurisdictional work involving collaboration with specialist advisers in overseas jurisdictions and close engagement with clients and their wider advisory teams.
Your ongoing professional development will be supported by the breadth and complexity of the work, while you will also contribute actively to the team’s knowledge base. Our culture is collaborative and collegiate, with colleagues sharing expertise across the group and contributing to the development of our collective technical knowledge.
You will be part of a close-knit, supportive team focused on delivering outstanding advisory work for clients. Your expertise and contribution will be genuinely valued, and you will work with colleagues who care deeply about the quality of the advice we provide.
## Practice overview
Our Tax & Reward practice consists of nine partners, four Senior Counsels, 14 Senior Associates, 26 Associates, eight trainee solicitors and three Senior Knowledge Lawyers.
Our Tax & Reward group is rated as one of the leading tax advisory practices in the City. The group provides integrated tax advice for UK and international privately owned groups, combining corporate tax and private client expertise. Clients are often founder-led or family-controlled and face distinct tax, structuring and governance challenges. As with any tax practice in a City law firm, a proportion of our work is transaction-based, supporting corporate, financing, real estate and investment fund transactions, while a substantial and increasing part of our practice involves giving free-standing tax advice to clients of the group.
## The role
The successful candidate will undertake a broad range of high-quality work across the tax practice. Core responsibilities will include:
* Ability to perform at a high level on complex advisory matters for group and international clients, across a wide range of UK and cross-border tax issues. This includes advising on tax-efficient structuring of domestic and international operations, group reorganisations, demergers, returns of value and ownership restructuring, as well as planning and strategy for international tax developments.
* **Client Management:** Delivering excellent client service and managing matters end-to-end (with appropriate delegation), operating with minimal supervision and acting as a trusted point of contact for clients. You will work directly with high-value private groups and their wider advisory teams on sophisticated, often multi-jurisdictional, engagements – including matters involving corporate tax, employment tax and personal tax dimensions.
* **Technical Excellence:** Producing high-quality, well-reasoned tax advice across a range of advisory matters, including residence and domicile issues, governance across jurisdictions, transfer pricing, diverted profits tax, and multi-jurisdictional tax risk management. The role also involves working alongside our private client teams on succession planning, estate and inheritance tax strategy for founders and families, and multi-generational transitions.
* **Team Development:** Playing a material role in the development of junior associates by leading and supervising on client matters, sharing technical expertise, and actively contributing to the team's knowledge base, collective expertise and training programme.
This job description encompasses the main duties of the role and is by no means exhaustive. It is anticipated that duties may vary from time to time according to the needs of the practice area.
## The candidate
We are seeking a Senior Associate to join Macfarlanes' Tax team, working within the group and international tax practice led by Greg Price and Sarah Ling. This is a highly technical role requiring a well-rounded individual with significant advisory experience across a broad range of tax matters.
* minimum of five years' PQE or equivalent post training professional experience;
* a broad spectrum of tax advisory experience; and
* demonstrated ability to manage client matters and effectively supervise and delegate to associates and trainees.
The ideal candidate will bring substantial experience in a senior capacity within one or more of the following environments:
* **Government:** HMRC or HM Treasury, with a focus on international tax policy and large business matters.
* **Professional Services:** A Big 4 or other leading accountancy firm, operating at Senior Manager level or above within a recognised international tax advisory practice. Candidates should have worked predominantly on international tax advisory matters and/or corporate M&A transactions, rather than compliance or audit engagements.
* **Legal:** A reputable law firm, where they will have gained significant responsibility and exposure to high-quality, complex international tax work.

Any offer of employment with us is subject to our pre-employment checks which are conducted by a third-party screening provider. These may include but are not limited to your professional and academic qualifications, any criminal records and employment references. These checks will be initiated with your consent and your offer will be subject to the successful completion of these checks.

Inclusion is one of our key priorities and it is a goal we are actively working towards. We believe that an inclusive, forward-thinking culture is intrinsically important and enables us to provide innovative solutions to our clients.
We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, bringing different perspectives and experiences, making Macfarlanes an exciting and stimulating place to work. Our teams have used Java, Ruby, Python, ES6 with React, as well as C# with .NET Core. We don’t limit ourselves as a company and we expect all our Engineers to be keen on learning new technologies. Automation is important to our teams, so we make sure there is a CD pipeline set up to build, test, and release many times per day.
High performing software delivery teams need to be empowered to iteratively and rapidly deliver changes all the way through to production. To do this we combine our extensive cloud automation knowledge with DevOps culture.
We ensure we document our architecture and infrastructure as code, using technologies such as Terraform and OpenAPI. Containerisation is a big part of empowering our teams to develop, deploy and scale their applications, but so too is using AWS Lambda and avoiding the complexity of stateful services altogether. Right tool for the job.
For us, DevOps is about culture rather than roles and titles. Even though this role is for someone with strong DevOps experience, the biggest impact you will have is coaching and helping teams use the platforms you build. You won't be building infrastructure in isolation or charged with deploying other peoples work into production. You'll empower teams with the mantra: you build it, you run it!
We grow a team of language agnostic engineers, which you might already consider yourself to be, who are versed in a mix of paradigms such as object-oriented, functional, declarative, event-based and aspect-oriented. To create this environment our Senior Software Engineers need to embrace sharing their knowledge and skills with others, and they need to keep an open mind – we’d love to hear some examples of mentoring, coaching and growing team members. Maybe you will have written some blog posts about your discipline, or perhaps even delivered a talk or two.

job_description:
As a Senior Claims Adjuster in the Marine Short Tail team, you will be joining as an integral part of the Markel London Market claims team. Reporting into the Assistant Claims Manager, you will be responsible for leading and driving claims forward in a proactive manner. Markel is a people powered company and we value our relationships, not just with our customers, but with all of the stakeholders in the claims process. Your role will be key in maintaining these relationships and promoting our Claims Value Proposition by providing a market leading service. We’re all about people | We win together | We strive for better | We enjoy the everyday | We think further
**Who we are:**
**Business Unit overview:**
The Claims department seeks to be a market-leader in the provision of an efficient, cost-effective and professional service to our brokers and clients. Our vision is to be the most customer centric, nimble and value adding claims team in the market. We strive to be pro-active and flexible in the management of claims whilst maintaining our integrity. The claims team works collaboratively alongside the underwriting function in order to facilitate close communication and exchange of ideas, and is an integral part of the product and customer service delivered to our clients. The Marine Short Tail team handle a broad range of claims emanating from the Marine Cargo, Specie, Hull & War Underwriting Division. Part of Markel Group (NYSE – MKL) a Fortune 500 company with over 60 offices in 20+ countries, is a holding company for insurance, reinsurance, specialist advisory, and investment operations around the world.
**What you’ll be doing:**
* Drive, through your own work the claim's philosophy of being “The most customer focused, nimble and value adding claims team in the market”. Achieve this through: agreeing, reviewing and completing your own objectives; your contribution at team meetings; effective oversight of DCAs and service providers; and interaction with key brokers. Passing back any key information in this regard to your team.
* Be responsible for handling your claims in accordance with the MINT claims and reserving philosophy, Markel Style, the Claims Handling Manual and all regulatory and legislative requirements. Calling out claims to your manager, where appropriate, for input on strategy and/or reserving.
* Drive, facilitate and deliver a customer focused approach to claims which is measurable through speed of service and open, honest and personable communications with all brokers and (re)insureds.
* Produce good quality and informative narratives and information on key claims and claims developments, and to ensure this is brought up as appropriate to management (whether to your direct manager or beyond), including provision of narratives for inclusion in your team's monthly/quarterly reports.
* Work closely with the underwriting team, including providing feedback on claims experiences, contract wordings, claims data or feedback for any renewal or new business and interact with placing and claims brokers to develop strong relationships and knowledge about the quality of our claims management at Markel. Work collaboratively with our Actuarial and Outwards Reinsurance teams, ensuring that they are all informed of new notifications and significant developments.
* Show a willingness to lead claims on all classes of business handled by the team, including attending underwriting meetings, learning about the class and developing relationships with key collaborators.
**Key Skills:**
* Take the lead and management of strategy on a portfolio of complex and/or high value claims and be a point person to the relevant underwriters. Identify and discuss the most common areas and trends in claims causation. Segment and analyse the portfolio to assist in identifying the most profitable sub-segments and those areas where remedial action should be taken. Understand, monitor, provide feedback and ensure compliance on KPIs.
* Analyse and interpret data to improve Markel’s underwriting capabilities (e.g. loss performance and underwriting efficiency). Scope out problems/questions for analysis and work with actuarial/underwriting/claims manager or head of class to investigate.
* Assist underwriters with the development of policy language to achieve desired coverage and propose wording amendments to manager and/or underwriters.
* Consistently produce quality work, finding the most efficient and practical means of overcoming challenges and demonstrating effective organisational skills.
* Understand customer needs and actively solicit and act upon feedback, providing solutions to problems. Form relationships outside of the claim's function including UW’s, brokers and key legal providers.
* Negotiate complex coverage matters calmly and effectively in the interests of all parties. Competently represent MINT in the management of market and broker meetings.
* Assist in the training of junior members of the claims team. Providing insight into specific claims aspects and helping them develop their own capabilities.
* Background and knowledge in Fine Art & Specie is required. Also, knowledge of Marine Cargo is desired.
* You will have achieved ACII accreditation, or be working towards it.

The Manager, Agriculture, Allergens & Nutrition is accountable for the leadership and development of the Agriculture, Allergens and Nutrition function, setting a clear direction, building capability and ensuring successful delivery of McDonald’s UK & Ireland priorities and the >NEXT strategy.
